  • Now let not your mind be outgoing; turn it inward; control it just a little ( Its like you need to clear the water, but not disturb it ) and watch for the Self, always remembering that the investigator is himself the essence of being and the Self of self. This tells us what to do, what not to do and what to engage in.
  • Be also free from the thought “I see” ; remain still like a blind man seeing. What transcends sight and no sight, That you are. Be quick and be That. Let that feeling of “I see” vanish as well. In that state absolutely unstained by will, sensation or thought, stay there.
  • Now, he goes into Nirvikalpa Samadhi.

Final emancipation sahaja samadhi

  • Now, he just wants to close his eyes and go to that state again and again.
  • She realizes his eagerness to go into that state again. She asks him what happens when he closes his eyes vs when he leaves it open.
  • He tells her to leave him stay in that blissful state and even tells her why she would live outside in vain, when she could be living in that bliss.
  • Comes the Brahmastra: Your small measure of wisdom is as good as no wisdom, because it is not unconditional, but remains conditioned by closing or opening your eyes. How ridiculous to think that your eyelid, one inch long, can shut up the expanse in which millions of worlds revolve in one corner alone!
  • She tells him about knots of entanglement and asks him: The state which is the result of your closing the eyes cannot be enough, for it is pure intelligence and eternal truth transcending anything else yet serving as the magnificent mirror to reflect the phenomena arising in itself. Prove, if you can, that everything is not contained in it.
  • Therefore I tell you that your conviction, ‘I shall lose it by opening my eyes’ , or ‘I know it’ , is the knot waiting to be cut. Remember, it cannot be the perfect state if it can be attained.
  • Fire of realization will burn away all your sense of duty so that there will be nothing left for you to do. Root out your thoughts, cut off the deep-rooted knots from your heart, namely, “I will see”, “I am not this”, “This is non-self”, and such alike.
  • Hemachuda finally cleared his confusion and got established in self within and without. Then they led a kingdom together doing everything they had to do like engaging in wars etc. Led the life of virtue studying scriptures and teaching them to others as well. Lived a Jivanmukta.
  • The Rishis, Sanaka and others, called it the Renowned City of Wisdom when they visited it.

Knots of entanglement

  • Identification of body with the self, thus stuck in perennial stream of happiness and misery in the shape of the cycle of births and deaths.
  • The differentiation of the world from the Self.
  • The differentiation of beings among themselves and from the universal Self.

Hemalekha’s teachings

  • Pleasure and pain is relative to circumstance. Fire gives pleasure and pain according to seasons, places, and its own size or intensity. Such relative thing is always tinged with misery. Same relative idea applies to cold, to wife, to sons, to kingdom and so on.
  • Misery is of two kinds: external and internal. External misery pertains to the body and is caused by the nerves, etc.; and internal pertains to the mind and is caused by desire.
  • Mental distraction is worse than physical pain and the whole world has fallen a victim to it. Desire is the seed of the tree of misery and never fails in its fruits.
  • Even Indra and the Devas, are still slaves to desire, and work day and night according to its dictates.
  • Same embrace by the beloved feels happy in one circumstance, and unhappy in the other. After copulation, fatigue occurs for everybody like fatigue for an animal carrying a load. How do you see that as happiness?
  • The friction of nadis is same for man as it is for a dog. If it is because of the beauty of the beloved, then that is produced by mere fanciful notion, and similar to union with a woman in a dream.
  • Beauty is just a concept of the mind. The fair woman that appears as the object is only the reflection of subtle concept already inside the subjective mind.
  • The mind draws an image of her beauty in conformity with its own repeated conceptions. Makes it clear and clear until it appears solidly as the object. Attraction springs up and enslaves the mind by constant mental associations.
  • The mind, becoming restless, stirs up the senses and seeks the fulfilment of its desires in the object.
  • Repeated mental picture is the reason for infatuation. Yogis and children do not dwell on such things, so are not excited in the same way. Whoever finds pleasure in anything, the beauty therein is only mental imagery. Fie on human beings who appraise the foulest part of the body as the most delightful. If one should see beauty in that bodily part which is wet with impure excretions, where would he not see beauty?
  • If, on the other hand, beauty is natural to the object of love, why is it not recognised by children too, as sweetness in edibles is recognised by them?
  • Though the prince heard these words from his wife and developed disgust for them, the force of habit still remained with him. He was therefore unable either to enjoy himself or to desist all of a sudden. This is the natural state of things: mind is a slave of habits, so as long as there are prints that were reinforced inside the mind, one is still a slave.
  • Disharmony of tempers cause disease in the body.
  • The prince told his wife after a long time why he felt diseased. He told her that he can no longer find anything to make him happy. “Just as a man under orders to be executed cannot relish the luxuries provided for him by the State, so also I do not relish anything.”
  • From that, the wife recognized that the seed of dispassion was laid within him. That state of dispassion only arises in one with whose continued devotion to Tripura, inherent in the Heart as the Self, is well pleased. Now, she tells him the gist in the form of a story.

Dissection of faculties

The story Hemalekha told the prince

Formerly, my mother gave me a lady-in-waiting who was good by nature, but later associated with an undesirable friend.

This friend was clever in creating new and wonderful things. I also without my mother’ s knowledge associated with her.

That lady-in-waiting became very friendly with that undesirable companion, and I was obliged to do the same because I loved my friend more than life.

I could not remain without her even for a second; so much did she enthral me by her undoubted purity.

Always loving my friend, I quickly became part of herself. She for her part was all the time close to her friend, a wicked strumpet, who was ever generating new and fascinating things.

In secret that woman introduced her son to my friend. That son was an ignorant fool with eyes bloodshot with drink. And my friend went on enjoying him in my very presence. But she, though completely overpowered by him and being enjoyed by him day after day, never left me, and I, too, did not abandon her. And out of that union was born a fool, of the same type as his father.

He grew up to be a very restless young fellow, fully inheriting his father’ s dullness and his grandmother’ s wickedness and creativeness. This boy, Master Inconstant by name, was brought up and trained by his father, Mr. Fool and his grandmother Madame Ignorance, and he became skilled in their ways. He could negotiate the most difficult places with perfect ease and surmount obstacles in a trice.

In this manner, my friend, though very good by nature, became afflicted and silly because of her association with wicked people.

What with love for her friend, devotion for her lover, and affection for her son, she began gradually to forsake me. But I could not break with her so easily.

Not being self-reliant, I was dependent on her and so remained with her.

Her husband, Mr. Fool, though always in enjoyment of her, mistook me for one of the same sort and tried to ravish me. But I was not what he took me to be. I am pure by nature and only led by her, for the time being.

Even so, there was widespread scandal about me in the world, that I was always in Mr. Fool’ s hold.

My friend, entrusting her son Master Inconstant to me, was always in the company of her lover.

Mr. Inconstant grew up in my care and in due course married a wife with his mother’ s approval.

Unsteady by name, she was ever restless and changeful and could put on different forms to please her husband’ s whim.

By her wonderful capacity to change and by her exceeding skill and cleverness, she brought her husband completely under her control.

Mr. Inconstant, too, used to fly hundreds of miles in a twinkling of an eye and return, go here, there and everywhere, but yet could find no rest.

Whenever Mr. Inconstant wished to go anywhere and whatever he wanted to have in any measure, Madame Unsteady was ready to meet his desires, changing herself accordingly and creating new environments to please her husband. She thus won his affections entirely.

She bore him five sons who were devoted to their parents. Each one was skilled in his own way. They were also entrusted to my care by my friend.

Out of love for my friend, I brought them up with care, and made them strong. Then those five sons of Madam Unsteady individually erected splendid palaces, invited their father to their homes and entertained him continually in turns.

The eldest of them entertained him in his mansion with different kinds of sweet music, with incantations of the Vedas, the reading of scriptures, the humming sounds of bees, the twittering of birds and other sounds sweet to hear. The father was pleased with the son, who arranged for still further sounds for him which were harsh, fearful and tumultuous like the roar of the lion, the peal of thunder, the raging of the sea, the rumblings of earthquakes, the cries from lying-in-chambers, and the quarrels, moans and lamentations of many people.

Invited by his second son, the father went to stay in his mansion. There he found soft seats, downy beds, fine clothes and some hard things; others hot or warm or cold, or refreshing things with various designs, and so on. He was pleased with the agreeable things and felt aversion to the disagreeable ones.

Then going to the third son, he saw charming and variegated scenes, things red, white, brown, blue, yellow, pink, smoky-grey, tawny, red-brown, black and spotted, others fat or lean, short or long, broad or round, bent or wavy, pleasing or horrible, nauseous, brilliant or savage, unsightly or captivating, some pleasing and others otherwise.

The father was taken to the fourth son’ s mansion and there he had fruits and flowers to order. He had drinks, things to be licked, to be sucked, and to be masticated; juicy things, some refreshing like nectar, others sweet, sour, pungent or astringent, some decoctions of similar flavours, and so on. He tasted them all.

The last son took the father to his home and treated him with fruits and flowers, with various scented grasses, herbs and things of different odours, sweet or putrescent, mild or acrid; others stimulating or soporific and so on.

In this manner, he enjoyed himself uninterruptedly, one way or another, in one mansion or another, being pleased with some and repulsed by others.

The sons too were so devoted to their father that they would not touch anything themselves in his absence.

But Mr. Inconstant not only enjoyed himself thoroughly in his sons’ mansions, but also stole away things from them and shared them in secret with his dear wife, Madam Unsteady, in his own home, unknown to his sons.

I too continued to live there because of my love for my friend. Otherwise, none of them could remain in the town without me who was their protectress, though I was moribund owing to my friend’ s moribundity.

When my friend’ s son retired to rest, he always slept soundly on the lap of his mother; as Mr. Inconstant was asleep, all others, including his sons, were also asleep, for no one could remain awake.

On such occasions, the city was guarded by Mr. Motion, the intimate friend of Mr. Inconstant, who was always moving to and fro by two upper gateways.

My friend, the mother of Mr. Inconstant, along with him and her wicked friend — the same was her mother-in-law — watched the whole sleeping family.

I used to seek my mother in that interval and remain blissful in her fond embrace. But I was obliged to return to the city simultaneously with the waking of the sleepers.

This Mr. Motion, the friend of Mr. Inconstant, is most powerful and keeps them all alive. Though single, he multiplies himself, manifests as the city and citizens, pervades them all, protects and holds them. Without him, they would all be scattered and lost like pearls without the string of the necklace. He is the bond between the inmates and myself; empowered by me, he serves in the city as the string in a necklace. If that city decays, he collects the inmates together, leads them to another and remains their master.

In this way Mr. Inconstant rules over cities always, he himself remaining under the sway of his friend. Though supported by such a powerful friend, though born of such a virtuous mother and brought up by me, he is never otherwise than miserable, because he is tossed about by his two wives and several sons.

He is torn asunder by his sons and finds not the least pleasure but only intense misery. Tempted by Madam Unsteady, he grieves; ordered about by Madam Vorax, he runs about in search of food for her; stricken by Flaming-mouth he burns with rage, loses his sense and is baffled; approaching Master Mean, he is openly despised and reviled by others and becomes as one dead under the shame of odium.

Who can hope for even the least happiness in bad company? One may as well seek to quench one’ s thirst by drinking water from a mirage.

Engulfed in sorrow, my friend once sought me in private. Advised by me, she soon gained a good husband, killed her own son and imprisoned his sons.

Then accompanied by me, she quickly gained my mother’ s presence, and being pure, she often embraced my mother. She at once dived in the sea of Bliss and became Bliss itself. In the same manner, you too can conquer your wrong ways which are only accretions.

The revelation of the mystery

My mother -> Transcendence ( Pure Consciousness ) My friend -> Intellect ( Discerning Faculty ) Undesirable friend of my friend aka Madam Dark -> Ignorance Undesirable friend’s son, my friend’s lover -> Delusion Master Inconstant -> Mind Daughter in Law of Madam Dark -> Dream Mrs. Changeful -> Changeful Madam Vorax -> Desire Madam Vorax Sons -> Anger and Greed Guard that keeps watch -> Breath Five sons of Mr. Inconstant -> Five sense organs

Actions and their meaning revealed:

  • Sharing stolen objects with his wife is the manifestation of proclivities in dreams.
  • What was said to be my most potent talisman is Realisation of the Self.
  • Mind’ s friend guarding the city is the vital principle which keeps moving as the life-breath. ( The main guard of the city that keeps watch )
  • The different cities peopled by them are hells passed in the eternal passage of the soul.
  • The consummation of the discerning faculty is samadhi.
  • My admission into my mother’ s chamber is final emancipation.

More comments on those:

  • Delusion tried to overpower me, but I remained pure. Still, the phantasmagoria pertaining to Intellect were attributed to me — individual Consciousness.
  • He, with his grandmother’ s permission (i.e., guided by ignorance), took Changeful for his wife. Mind enjoyed himself with her because she could satisfy him in every way. The five Senses were born of this couple.
  • The Senses functioned in the sensory organs and their father — Mind — was able to project himself through them and enjoy himself thoroughly. His enjoyments gave him pleasure just at the moment, and left their impressions on him, which he took with him in order to manifest them in the dream state and enjoy them secretly with his wife, unknown to the gross senses.
  • Desire possessed the mind and fed him to his entire satisfaction. His desire grew more and more until neither he nor all his associates could satisfy Desire. Constant association of Mind with Desire gave rise to Passion and Greed (the two sons of the second wife). Desire was exceedingly fond of her two sons. Mind was however tortured by these two sons.
  • Mind’ s misery was reflected in the Intellect. I (the individual Consciousness) was completely hidden behind the dark and active forces dragging the intellect along and appeared moribund. Suffering thus for untold ages, the Mind lost all initiative and was in the clutches of Desire. Then he gained, at the time of creation, a city of ten gates — namely the body with ten outlets (two eyes, two ears, two nasal passages, mouth, urinary and faecal passages and brahmarandhra, an opening in the skull).
  • My sisters are infinite in number, like the waves of the sea. All of them are involved like myself in their companion’ s affairs. Though so enmeshed in Intellect, I am still equal to my mother in every respect because I possess the unique talisman to save me from being tainted.
  • To return to my life in the city, whenever Mind was fatigued, he used to sleep on his mother Intellect’ s lap. When he slept, none of his sons or others could be awake. The city was then guarded by his intimate friend, Breath. Then Intellect with all her family used to be clouded by Ignorance — her mother-in-law and then I (individual Consciousness) being free from all trammels used to repair to my mother (i.e., Fullness) and remain in bliss. But I was obliged to come away as soon as the inhabitants of the city awoke.
  • When that city fell to ruin, he would collect them all and pass with them to another city. Mind thus reigned in several places, with the aid of his friend (this refers to reincarnation)
  • Though befriended by Breath, though born of virtuous Intellect and though brought up by me, Mind was always wallowing in misery because he was wedded to his two incorrigible and insatiate wives, associated with the two wicked sons — Greed and Anger — and was swinging to and fro on account of the other five sons — the Senses.
  • His miseries reflected on Intellect; and I too being associated with her, was involved in their woes. Who can indeed avoid the evils of bad company?
  • On one occasion, Intellect sought my advice in secret (i.e., when accidentally free from thoughts). I advised dispassionate conduct to her, by which she gained a good husband — Discrimination. She grew stronger, gathered courage to subdue the Mind and kill Greed, Lust and Anger. The other five sons of his — namely, the Senses — were imprisoned. Soon after, she became loyal to me and finally united with me (i.e., gained nirvikalpa samadhi). Thus she reached my mother’ s home — Peace and Bliss.

My initial guesses were this upto the negotiate part:

Mother -> Pure Awareness Lady in Waiting -> Body Undesirable Friend -> Thought ( Said to be creative as well ) Undesirable Friend’s son -> Mind Thought fell in love with Mr Mind. From mind and thought, came Reasoning Mr. Inconstant. That explains its negotiating power.

The prince’s complaints to hemalekha

  • But the infatuated prince noticed that Hemalekha was not as amorous as himself. Feeling that she was always unresponsive, he asked her in private: My dear! How is it you are not as attentive to me as I am to you? Thou fairest of girls, radiant with smiles! How is it that you are never keen on seeking pleasure or enjoying it? Are not these pleasures to your taste?
  • Even when I am close to you, your mind seems to be elsewhere; when spoken to, you do not seem to listen. As I hold you in close embrace for a long while, you seem unconscious of me, and then ask me, Lord, when did you come?
  • Shortly afterwards he pulled himself together and began to reflect as follows: Shame on me who am so addicted to drink! Shame on the fools infatuated with love for women. Women are like nothing but birds flitting above the tree tops.

item.title: The Mind Divine
item.description: I wrote the poem Tentacles of Thoughts almost 8 years ago back when I was fighting a war with my own mind. It was brutal to see it through. I could have never imagined how my life would be in the next 8 years. The mind is like that double edged sword that it cuts everywhere it touches. Specially us when we don’t know what it is capable of. Yet in the hands of a skilled samurai, that katana is legendary. That comes from the will and discipline acting from that samurai towards the sword. Just like it, I have cut myself many thousand times over to wield this katana. And this poem is the katana writing about it’s journey:
item.content:
I wrote the poem Tentacles of Thoughts almost 8 years ago back when I was fighting a war with my own mind. It was brutal to see it through. I could have never imagined how my life would be in the next 8 years. The mind is like that double edged sword that it cuts everywhere it touches. Specially us when we don’t know what it is capable of. Yet in the hands of a skilled samurai, that katana is legendary. That comes from the will and discipline acting from that samurai towards the sword. Just like it, I have cut myself many thousand times over to wield this katana. And this poem is the katana writing about it’s journey:

 

The war was waged in a different light,

Fought the warriors of explosive might.

Wails and tears, and blood and bone,

Smell of death followed the empty throne.

 

Tired these warriors turned to sea,

Shackled by tentacles, yet, wanting to be free.

Tentacles followed them everywhere they went,

Some cut their limbs, while others felt faint.

 

    For those who survived and fled to the ocean, the ocean whispered:

 

Beneath the vast essence of sea,

Lay chests of treasure and coins.

Down on that ocean floor,

Hidden,

Forgotten,

Clogged by your tentacles yet again.

 

The shallow sea you warriors see,

No nectar, no flower for them lazy bee.

The oyster surfaces every full moon,

Only for the diver, who doesn’t give up soon.

 

No up, no down, no left, no right,

Neither is it dark down, nor is it bright.

Only for the diver who’s willing to fight,

I’ll catch you and show you this ocean’s might.

 

No stories, no tales, no right or wrong,

No sound, no silence, its far beyond.

No horror, no darkness, no hard, no pain

No cold, no peace, here only that remains.

 

Moved by your valor, let me show you the way

Teach you to dive deep, and see the eternal play.

There was no box, no ground, no death

All rising and falling in sync with your breath.

 

The warrior breathed deeply and watched the ocean.
After years, he finally understood and spoke back to the ocean:

 

I see you up, down, left and right,

Sound or silence, dark or bright,

Life or death, fight or flight,

I see you,

I adore you,

In all your glory, might and bright.

Adorned by my tentacles, oh’ what a sight,

I woke up as the ocean witnessing the fight.

item.title: Mindset for The "Uncertain" times
item.description:
If you think about world from diverse mental models and maps, you’ve already recognized that traditional structures in this world are falling. Be it Politics, Business, Education and so on. As if a switch was pressed, and it started getting more and more random. Ray Dalio has written a book on “The Changing World Order”. With close sensitive observation, its hard not to take a note.

The world is always in change without a doubt. But the important point of note is it remains relatively stable ( stale ) for decades or even centuries sometimes. Previously, money and leverage followed structure much more rigidly. Now, look at what altcoins and crypto is doing. Look at how influencer economy impacted our lives. One person is grinding their entire life saving pennies, and there’s another one who gains and loses like a gambling game. But if you look closely enough, its a form of barter we have accepted and used. So, you are a part of that gambling match whether you post your content publicly or not. Whether you know crypto or not. Big countries might adapt it, and a lot of lives change. Big countries make it illegal, and a lot of lives change too.
item.content:
If you think about world from diverse mental models and maps, you’ve already recognized that traditional structures in this world are falling. Be it Politics, Business, Education and so on. As if a switch was pressed, and it started getting more and more random. Ray Dalio has written a book on “The Changing World Order”. With close sensitive observation, its hard not to take a note.

The world is always in change without a doubt. But the important point of note is it remains relatively stable ( stale ) for decades or even centuries sometimes. Previously, money and leverage followed structure much more rigidly. Now, look at what altcoins and crypto is doing. Look at how influencer economy impacted our lives. One person is grinding their entire life saving pennies, and there’s another one who gains and loses like a gambling game. But if you look closely enough, its a form of barter we have accepted and used. So, you are a part of that gambling match whether you post your content publicly or not. Whether you know crypto or not. Big countries might adapt it, and a lot of lives change. Big countries make it illegal, and a lot of lives change too.

And that gambling match is getting more and more aggressive as the world is not clear about its order. Countries forming alliances, countries fighting within alliances. Revolutions, Trade Bans, Tariffs, Wars have spiked up in different places of the world. There were conflicts before, but now there’s no locus. Like a wildfire.

This is about the external world. Then comes our internal world. We think we have more choices in everything, then we get into “Paradox of Choice” making us delay choices and accept worse outcomes instead. Everyone looking for perfection that’s nowhere to be found outside. The ideals being defined by what we see in social media is making everyone restless. Everyone wants to reduce shame, yet be famous. Everyone wants to get good bits of asymmetry without the bad bits. That pulls us apart and tears us from the inside. It would undoubtedly have been better if our full society would have been kind and competent. In reality, we know that’s not the case. Most likely that it’ll never ever be fully so. Though a majority is kind, few get down to our nerves. One hate comment ruins like 10000s of good comments. That’s the asymmetry.

That’s why there is a huge influencer economy of incompetent advice. Promoting products that they never use, cult-like following and much more because of our incompetent behavior. We follow stupidly, that’s why most modern day influencers have a huge fan following. Then, when that stupidity turns into hate, it becomes very chaotic for the same person who enjoyed that asymmetry before. Influencers pretending a happy managed lifestyle making us feel even more miserable. How did we get here? Who are these seemingly “out-of-nowhere” experts? Excluding very few amazing people wanting to share their genuine expression of knowledge and art to the world. They are getting outshined by clickbait experts usually.

The career we study for in universities gets outdated faster than ever. New fields popping out randomly. Every new article says this job is at risk. That career is at risk, so on and so forth.

People think understanding what it is doesn’t help anything, but its not true. You have to understand the structure to break the structure apart safely. How do we deal with it then? Everything seems overwhelming. Everything seems fragile. Everything seems too random. Where is the answer?

The answer is in randomness itself. If you come from a Computer Science background, you study a sorting algorithm called “Quick Sort”. Quick Sort uses randomness to sort numbers efficiently. And you also probably know that quick sort isn’t opimal when the data is not very random. But given that the data is random and huge, that’s where it shines.

Think of all the modern information signals as random numbers. And you know there is chaos everywhere. And you know there are so many numbers that influence you. e.g. If you compare 30 years ago to today, just count the number of things that try to give information to your mind. For the period of a month, it surely has increased a million fold. So, bigger the randomness, the better it is for the algorithm that sorts it.

But what happens during a quick sort?

Quick sort “sort of” harnesses this randomness. It begins by selecting a pivot: a single element from the array that serves as its reference point. That can be any pivot. There is no rule to create a pivot. It’s not chosen for perfection but for its ability to divide the chaos into manageable parts. Numbers smaller than the pivot go left, larger ones go right. Then the process recurses on these subsets, partitioning again and again until order emerges from this disorder. This is not meant to be your Quick Sort Guide, just a short intro. These subsets are where we can still create some structure using our knowledge and understanding of randomness itself.

Example illustration:

But one key catch like I mentioned earlier is this: without randomness, Quick Sort can falter. On a more rigid traditional structure (like a nearly sorted list), poor pivot choices lead to unbalanced partitions, dragging efficiency down to a crawl. Introduce randomness—say, by randomly selecting the pivot—and the algorithm thrives, achieving near-optimal performance on average. So, the understanding is this: If there was a good structure that already had less randomness and jitter, you would have been well off by following traditional algorithms and patterns. In our case, careers and so on.

Understand this: The world is now best for people who have the courage to follow an unconventional path. For those who had nothing to lose, they gained more by risking it. It has happened since the beginning of time but the scale has significantly changed. One influencer earns maybe 1000x what a top physicist might earn by studying physics. Then if that same physicist works for a Quant Fund, then he earns 10-100x more than a normal physicist and so on. If a physicist studies Physics and has a Youtube channel too, he might be earning more from sharing on Youtube than from his research/job. So, we have to change for better. Instead of complaining, we have to master this chaos.

Summarzing all this, this is my personal advice: Reduce shame. Be more courageous. I know it’s easier said than done, but you’ve got nowhere that’s safe now. Courage won’t happen instantly, but you can work your way through. Start by playing around with pivots that need less courage and don’t provoke immediate fear-response. Then as you get more confident, you will increase stakes and play bigger & better games. Focus is an asymmetric skill when everyone is in fragmented. Calmness is an asymmetric skill when everyone is in panic. These meta-skills will turn out to be more helpful in times to come. Randomness breeds curiosity. Learn to use it like a mane, not to get caught up in it.

Just need to understand this final lesson from quick sort: you don’t keep changing pivots assuming that there can be a better pivot. You choose a pivot, divide it, and then start working on that subset. If each new information point ( number in our set. A reel in real life ) wants to keep changing pivot and not go to the immediate subsets, you fuck yourselves up. The algorithm never moves. It gets stuck on the first layer without any sorting. You get caught up in your own mess. Because choosing a pivot is for breaking it into subsets and working on those subsets. If you make choosing better pivot a game, then you are stuck infinitely in this randomness without getting anywhere.

Understand the randomness so that you can split it apart into manageable chunks and work on it. One random pivot, and structure can emerge without you even being aware that such a pivot/a point of leverage even exists in the first place. Try new things. Learn to switch quickly from one AI model to another without getting disrupted. Learn to break traditional learning methodologies with new developments in AI and LLMs. Learn about what works are being offered remotely. Invest in crypto randomly [ Given its legal in your country. It’s illegal in mine. ] ( Amount you can safely lose and you wouldn’t even know ). Do binge into random topics to know about structures that are building there. And invest before anyone else. This is the mindset I believe is needed for the future.

Those who keep updating their world models with each new development. Those who glide from one uncertainty to another without getting torn apart will be the ones who will shine in this new age. “Uncertainty is the new certainty until it changes with AGI.”

item.title: The Astronomy Book
item.description:
Timeline of discoveries

  • 2nd century BCE Aristarchus and one other astronomer believed in heliocentric model
  • 130 BCE : Hipparchus of Nicea noticed that star named Spica had moved 2 degrees east of the point of celestial sphere, called fall equinox point, compared to position recorded 150 years earlier. Then he found all stars position had shifted. This shift got known as “precession of the equinoxes”.
  • 15th century : Copernicus revives heliocentric model of solar system
  • 1748: Bradley discovered Nutation
  • 1814: A German maker of optical instruments named Joseph von Fraunhofer invented the spectroscope.
  • 1860: Kirchhoff showed that different patterns of dark lines are the spectral fingerprints of different chemical elements.
  • 1919: Rutherford transmuted atoms of N into O by firing particles at them from a radioactive element. That gave evidence to the fact that nuclear processes could produce new elements and release unimaginable quantities of energy.
  • 1979: Gravitational Lensing

Movement

  • A planet moves most rapidly when it is nearest the sun, at perihelion; a planet’s slowest motion occurs when it is farthest from the sun, at aphelion.
  • As an object’s velocity (v) approaches light speed (c), the object becomes increasingly squashed in the direction of travel when viewed by a stationary observer. This is not merely an illusion. In the observer’s frame of reference, the object’s shape really does change.
  • For example, the protons accelerated by the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) particle accelerator travel very close to the speed of light—within 99.999 percent. Additional energy does very little to this speed, and instead boosts mass. At full power, the protons in the LHC are nearly 7,500 times more massive than they were when stationary.
  • Slipher said that spiral nebulae were separate galaxies outside The Milky Way. Hubble used this result to confirm that the universe was expanding.

Sun

  • If the sun became a black hole, its event horizon would be 2 miles (3 km) from the center. A black hole with Earth’s mass would have a 1⁄3-in (9-mm) radius.
  • Payne in 1925 showed some crazy findings about heilum and hydrogen levels in stars which Henry Russell thought were crazy. Four years after, he conceded that she was right. And this established that most stars are chemically similar. She found way to determine temperature of any star from its spectrum. And showed that hydrogen and helium are dominant elements in universe - key step towards Big Bang Theory.
  • Since all gases obey the same laws, assuming that the sun is not only gaseous at the surface but throughout allows the calculation of the temperature and pressure at the center.
  • Einstein’s insight led many to revisit the idea that the universe started small, among them the Belgian priest Georges Lemaître, whose 1931 proposal would carry echoes of The Rigveda.

Telescope

  • With naked eye, the resolution that we see of moon is around 1/30.
  • With lens of 1, 2, 4 cm diameter, the resolution improves to 1/120, 1/240, 1/480 degrees respectively.

Bodies

  • Asteroids are irregular in shape if they have D < 380 km ( Hughes-Cole Limit )

  • Comet nuclei are among the darkest objects in the solar system. Only 4 percent of the light that falls on them is reflected. Fresh black asphalt, by comparison, reflects nearly twice as much.

  • The object that causes the glowing trail is called a meteor. If any of it survives to reach the ground, it is termed a meteorite.

  • Gravitational weight of a taller mountain would exceed the strength of the underlying mantle rock in case of Earth, that’s why we don’t have mountains bigger than Everest like 8.8km. So, in planets with lower mass, weight of objects is less, so there can be bigger mountains. e.g. Mars Mount Olympus is 3x higher than Everest. Mass of Mars is about 1/10th and diameter about 1/2 of Earth.

  • Small wobble in precession with an 18.6 year cycle. Both precession and nutation are caused by gravitational interactions between moon, earth and the sun.

  • Stars that changed in brightness with a regular period. Discovered by Goodricke with Delta Cephei star in constellation of Cepheus.

    • Cepheid variables are reasonably easy to recognize because they are among the brightest variable stars, and they have a characteristic light curve, showing fairly rapid increases in brightness followed by a slower tailing off. Today, they are known to be giant yellow stars that “pulsate”—varying in diameter as well as brightness over their cycles—and are very rare.
    • Hertzsprung proposed that there was a definite relationship between periods and average intrinsic brightness. Then by comparing its intrinsic brightness to its apparent magnitude (measured average brightness from Earth), it should be possible to calculate the distance to the Cepheid variable.
    • Using statistical parallax, he tried to calculate distances to Cepheids in the Milky way galaxy.
    • 1923 : Hubble measured distance to Cepheid in the Andromeda galaxy leading to understanding that Andromeda nebula was a different galaxy.
    • The star RS Puppis is one of the brightest Cepheid variables in the Milky Way. It is about 6,500 light-years from Earth and has a cycle of variability lasting 41.4 days.
    • Today, classical Cepheids are used to measure the distance of galaxies out to about 100 million light-years—well beyond the local group of galaxies.
    • Classical Cepheids have also been used to clarify many characteristics of the Milky Way galaxy, such as its local spiral structure and the sun’s distance from the plane of the galaxy. Type II Cepheids have been used to measure distances to galactic center and globular clusters.
    • These stars expand and contract over a regular cycle, at the same time regularly varying in brightness. They are hottest and brightest shortly after reaching their most contracted phase. The graph of the star’s luminosity (light output) against time is called its light curve.

  • Many meteorites contain small particles called chondrules. Some of the oldest materials in solar system and can tell about meteorite’s early composition.

  • Orbital resonance occurs when the gravity of orbiting bodies produces a stable and self-correcting system. An example is the orbits of the neighboring giant planets Jupiter and Saturn, whose orbital periods are in a ratio of 5:2.

  • Parallax is the apparent movement of a nearby object against distant objects due to the changing position of the observer.

  • It was discovered that there are long periods in each cycle when the number of sunspots is low.

  • Edward Pickering employed a large team of women to carry out the work of classification of stars based on temperature sequence.

Timeline of discoveries

  • 2nd century BCE Aristarchus and one other astronomer believed in heliocentric model
  • 130 BCE : Hipparchus of Nicea noticed that star named Spica had moved 2 degrees east of the point of celestial sphere, called fall equinox point, compared to position recorded 150 years earlier. Then he found all stars position had shifted. This shift got known as “precession of the equinoxes”.
  • 15th century : Copernicus revives heliocentric model of solar system
  • 1748: Bradley discovered Nutation
  • 1814: A German maker of optical instruments named Joseph von Fraunhofer invented the spectroscope.
  • 1860: Kirchhoff showed that different patterns of dark lines are the spectral fingerprints of different chemical elements.
  • 1919: Rutherford transmuted atoms of N into O by firing particles at them from a radioactive element. That gave evidence to the fact that nuclear processes could produce new elements and release unimaginable quantities of energy.
  • 1979: Gravitational Lensing

  • With lens of 1, 2, 4 cm diameter, the resolution improves to 1/120, 1/240, 1/480 degrees respectively.

So, in planets with lower mass, weight of objects is less, so there can be bigger mountains. e.g. Mars Mount Olympus is 3x higher than Everest. Mass of Mars is about 1/10th and diameter about 1/2 of Earth.

  • Small wobble in precession with an 18.6 year cycle. Both precession and nutation are caused by gravitational interactions between moon, earth and the sun.

  • Stars that changed in brightness with a regular period. Discovered by Goodricke with Delta Cephei star in constellation of Cepheus.

Today, they are known to be giant yellow stars that “pulsate”—varying in diameter as well as brightness over their cycles—and are very rare.
    • Hertzsprung proposed that there was a definite relationship between periods and average intrinsic brightness. Then by comparing its intrinsic brightness to its apparent magnitude (measured average brightness from Earth), it should be possible to calculate the distance to the Cepheid variable.
    • Using statistical parallax, he tried to calculate distances to Cepheids in the Milky way galaxy.
    • 1923 : Hubble measured distance to Cepheid in the Andromeda galaxy leading to understanding that Andromeda nebula was a different galaxy.
