item.title: Zen and Art of Motorcycle Maintenance
item.description:
Quotes

We want to make good time, but for us now this is measured with emphasis on ‘good’ rather than ‘time’ and when you make that shift in emphasis the whole approach changes.

In a car you’re always in a compartment, and because you’re used to it you don’t realize that through that car window everything you see is just more TV. You’re a passive observer and it is all moving by you boringly in a frame. On a cycle the frame is gone. You’re completely in contact with it all. You’re in the scene, not just watching it anymore, and the sense of presence is overwhelming.
item.content:
Quotes

We want to make good time, but for us now this is measured with emphasis on ‘good’ rather than ‘time’ and when you make that shift in emphasis the whole approach changes.

In a car you’re always in a compartment, and because you’re used to it you don’t realize that through that car window everything you see is just more TV. You’re a passive observer and it is all moving by you boringly in a frame. On a cycle the frame is gone. You’re completely in contact with it all. You’re in the scene, not just watching it anymore, and the sense of presence is overwhelming.

The truth knocks on the door and you say, ‘Go away, I’m looking for the truth,’ and so it goes away.

The whole pace of life and personality of the people who live along them (shortcuts to the main highways) are different. They’re not going anywhere. They’re not too busy to be courteous. The hereness and nowness of things is something they know all about.

Now the stream of our common consciousness seems to be obliterating its own banks, losing its central direction and purpose, flooding the lowlands, disconnecting and isolating the highlands and to no particular purpose other than the wasteful fulfillment of its own internal momentum.

What it’s for you don’t know, and why it’s there, there’s no one to tell, and so all you can feel is alienated, estranged, as though you didn’t belong there.

I just think that their flight from and hatred of technology is self-defeating. The Buddha, the Godhead, resides quite as comfortably in the circuits of a digital computer or the gears of a cycle transmission as he does at the top of a mountain or in the petals of a flower.

I argued that physical discomfort is important only when the mood is wrong. Then you fasten on to whatever thing is uncomfortable and call that the cause.

You can’t really think hard about what you’re doing and listen to the radio at the same time. Maybe they didn’t see their job as having anything to do with hard thought, just wrench twiddling. If you can twiddle wrenches while listening to the radio that’s more enjoyable.

When you want to hurry something, that means you no longer care about it and want to get on to other things.

Each machine has its own, unique personality which probably could be defined as the intuitive sum total of everything you know and feel about it. This personality constantly changes, usually for the worse, but sometimes surprisingly for the better, and it is this personality that is the real object of motorcycle maintenance.

Someone’s ungrateful and you tell him he’s ungrateful, okay, you’ve called him a name. You haven’t solved anything.

Summary

I feel like he had a list of quotes that truly represent Zen first and then wrote the story to obscure these intentionally. I say that while reading the book I didn’t find it that profound, just talking about his motorcycle maintenance, problems and so on. But now while I am reviewing my highlights, it doesn’t feel that shallow. Zen is vey easy to say profoundly because the obvious nature of it is contradictions and depth. And anything can seem deep if you just use heavy words. The beauty of Zen is in the depth that arises alongside simplicity. There is no enough of Zen, but I feel like I have arrived at that simplicity by stripping away my complexities. I think it can be a good book for Zen beginners but they will need to read twice to see a bit of Zen.

Highlights

The reader does not see that the governess is the villainess because what the governess sees is all the reader ever sees

It was some years ago that my wife and I and our friends first began to catch on to these roads. We took them once in a while for variety or for a shortcut to another main highway, and each time the scenery was grand and we left the road with a feeling of relaxation and enjoyment. We did this time after time before realizing what should have been obvious: these roads are truly different from the main ones. The whole pace of life and personality of the people who live along them are different. They’re not going anywhere. They’re not too busy to be courteous. The hereness and nowness of things is something they know all about

The truth knocks on the door and you say, ‘Go away, I’m looking for the truth,’ and so it goes away. Puzzling

We’re in such a hurry most of the time we never get much chance to talk. The result is a kind of endless day-to-day shallowness, a monotony that leaves a person wondering years later where all the time went and sorry that it’s all gone

Now the stream of our common consciousness seems to be obliterating its own banks, losing its central direction and purpose, flooding the lowlands, disconnecting and isolating the highlands and to no particular purpose other than the wasteful fulfillment of its own internal momentum. Some channel deepening seems called for

It is as though two old friends, a Catholic and a Protestant, were sitting drinking beer, enjoying life, and the subject of birth control somehow came up. Big freeze-out

And the more I probe and push on this subject of cycle maintenance the more irritated he gets, and of course that makes me want to probe and push all the more. Not deliberately to irritate him but because the irritation seems symptomatic of something deeper, something under the surface that isn’t immediately apparent

You can prove the practicality of planned parenthood till you get tired of listening to yourself and it’s going to go nowhere because your antagonist isn’t buying the assumption that anything socially practical is good per se. Goodness for him has other sources which he values as much as or more than social practicality

And the more I try to fathom what makes me enjoy mechanical work and them hate it so, the more elusive it becomes. The ultimate cause of this originally minor difference of opinion appears to run way, way deep

In a kind of singsong voice I repeated the plea for tuning and he tried hard to listen. He really tries hard sometimes. But then the block came again and he was off to the bar for another round for all of us and the subject was closed. He is not stubborn, not narrow-minded, not lazy, not stupid. There was just no easy explanation. So it was left up in the air, a kind of mystery that one gives up on because there is no sense in just going round and round and round looking for an answer that’s not there

What struck me hard then was that she was not blaming the faucet, and that she was deliberately not blaming the faucet. She wasn’t ignoring the faucet at all! She was suppressing anger at that faucet and that goddamned dripping faucet was just about killing her! But she could not admit the importance of this for some reason

Anything to do with valves and shafts and wrenches is a part of that dehumanized world, and they would rather not think about it. They don’t want to get into it

Clichés and stereotypes such as ‘beatnik’ or ‘hippie’ have been invented for the antitechnologists, the antisystem people, and will continue to be

I disagree with them about cycle maintenance, but not because I am out of sympathy with their feelings about technology. I just think that their flight from and hatred of technology is self-defeating. The Buddha, the Godhead, resides quite as comfortably in the circuits of a digital computer or the gears of a cycle transmission as he does at the top of a mountain or in the petals of a flower

Chris kept asking questions that started to anger me because he didn’t see how serious it was. Finally I saw it was no use, gave it up, and my anger at him disappeared. I explained to him as carefully as I could that it was all over

Two weeks after the vacation was over, one evening after work, I removed the carburetor to see what was wrong but still couldn’t find anything. To clean off the grease before replacing it, I turned the stopcock on the tank for a little gas. Nothing came out. The tank was out of gas. I couldn’t believe it. I can still hardly believe it. I have kicked myself mentally a hundred times for that stupidity and don’t think I’ll ever really, finally get over it. Evidently what I saw sloshing around was gas in the reserve tank which I had never turned on. I didn’t check it carefully because I assumed the rain had caused the engine failure. I didn’t understand then how foolish quick assumptions like that are. Now we are on a twenty-eight-horse machine and I take the maintenance of it very seriously

The radio was a clue. You can’t really think hard about what you’re doing and listen to the radio at the same time. Maybe they didn’t see their job as having anything to do with hard thought, just wrench twiddling. If you can twiddle wrenches while listening to the radio that’s more enjoyable

Not only did these mechanics not find that sheared pin, but it was clearly a mechanic who had sheared it in the first place, by assembling the side cover plate improperly. I remembered the previous owner had said a mechanic had told him the plate was hard to get on. That was why. The shop manual had warned about this, but like the others he was probably in too much of a hurry or he didn’t care.

On this trip I think we should notice it, explore it a little, to see if in that strange separation of what man is from what man does we may have some clues as to what the hell has gone wrong in this twentieth century. I don’t want to hurry it. That itself is a poisonous twentieth-century attitude. When you want to hurry something, that means you no longer care about it and want to get on to other things. I just want to get at it slowly, but carefully and thoroughly, with the same attitude I remember was present just before I found that sheared pin. It was that attitude that found it, nothing else

item.title: Satya Poem: After a decade
item.description:
The context is this: I wrote this poem as an extension of my emotions 10 years ago. The poem’s titled “Satya” and was the first poem on my blog.

Neither am I a poet, nor a storyteller. I wrote what I genuinely felt at that time. And this was close to when Gadhimai Mela was about to happen and there was a lot of news about Bali Pratha needing to stop and so on. It triggered something that was already brewing inside me vehemently, into words. This is my commentary on my own writing after 10 years of seeking, learning, and coming home.
item.content:
The context is this: I wrote this poem as an extension of my emotions 10 years ago. The poem’s titled “Satya” and was the first poem on my blog.

Neither am I a poet, nor a storyteller. I wrote what I genuinely felt at that time. And this was close to when Gadhimai Mela was about to happen and there was a lot of news about Bali Pratha needing to stop and so on. It triggered something that was already brewing inside me vehemently, into words. This is my commentary on my own writing after 10 years of seeking, learning, and coming home.

I will explain each paragraph one by one: what still is true, what I have learned that I didn’t a decade ago, and so on. This will probably be a long one, but a worthy one if you genuinely are looking for yourself too. And I don’t think I will write much on Spirituality from now on because my path is laid somewhere else. And there is more than enough written out there for an ardent seeker already.

I am just enjoying living. If you have questions, you can personally ask me. No time for arguments, all the time for those who truly need it. Apart from that, I hope you find peace within you. I bow down to the divinity in all of you. Lets get started here:

आकाङ्क्षाका पानाहरुमा
समेटिएको यो जीवनमा
च्यातिएका ती पानाहरु
स्वयमहित्को तान्डवसँगै
कुल्चिएका भावनाहरु ।

The wise ones say the Universe was born out of desire: a desire to find itself, know itself, know its limits. And so it does create these projections to understand what it can be. And that’s life summarized as well. And its true that each individual is fragmented, and torn; not because of themselves but by design. The same design that can recognize it as whole too. It’s just you who is unable to recognize this whole. To this, there is this Sanskrit quote that summarizes what you might not have known:

ॐ पूर्णमदः पूर्णमिदं पूर्णात्पूर्णमुदच्यते ।
पूर्णस्य पूर्णमादाय पूर्णमेवावशिष्यते ॥
ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः ॥

Meaning: This is complete, that is complete. From this whole, that whole arises.
When you take this whole out of that, it’s indeed complete yet again. Peace, Peace, Peace.

This is the idea. You don’t think that is possible because you didn’t assume the nature of this primordial whole which is uncaused. Just by being uncaused, its not graspable by logic. We understand linearity and causality pretty easily. You already know how brain fuck time travel movies can be. Think of it like that.
Think about the first thing that existed and how. Contemplate, introspect, and study at the same time. Whatever answer there is, it will find you.

So, coming to this, we who live our lives in misery, are these torn pages. This is not me saying it. This is Buddha saying “Life is misery”. And to why, everyone says its because you live too tight with your ego. Anything and everything hurts you. Your intuition, your emotions are bulldozered by someone else all the time. That’s why it is indeed miserable in general.

तिनै जलेका पानाहरु
धुँवा बनी उडेको छ
संसार जस्तो भएपनि
अदृश्यतामा रमेकोछ ।

Yes, the smell of misery is everywhere. The burnt smell is flowing here and there. We are all emitting that smell, and its almost as if it has engulfed the whole atmosphere. And where is the fragrance? The fragrance is hiding itself in the safest position away from the burnt smell: as fire that burns it. The smell of burning comes because you know there is somewhere fire that is burning. And that fire is your inner recognition: your inner peace lying within you. The smell that’s reaching your nose is telling you to look for that inner fire which has hidden itself but the symptom of that fire is that smell of burning itself.

हिमालका ती कोप्चारामा
हिउँसँगै जमेकोछ ।।

Yes, its frozen right there. Its not moving. Its still hiding behind that stiffness in all of us.

सुरको धुनमा बज्दा यसलाई
शब्दकोशमा खोजेपछि
आफुलाई नचाहरि
धर्मग्रन्थ रटेपछि
न्यायका ती किताबले नै
सत्यतालाई ढाकेपछि ।

This is one of these things one would say out of anger too. Beautiful words, but I didn’t know anything at that time. It just was written through my being. Neither did I know scriptures, nor did I know where the music was.

Its heavily true that you try to find words to expressions that you cannot understand. Like the origin of universe, there are things which logic can’t hold much longer, but your being knows exactly what its talking about.

If we both have experienced Love, we both understand a lover looking at the moon and appreciating the moon as their lovers. Or them looking at lover’s eyes and comparing it to the moon. We both didn’t communicate in words. We communicated in that imperfect expression of love which is pointing to the feeling that we understood in ourselves.

That is the same with inner Truth. It can’t be expressed in all these words I say. Even Rabindranath Tagore was not able to do it in Gitanjali. But when I read him, I see the same fragrance. Being which has touched the source at least, and wants to get engrossed in it.

In today’s world, not enough people are reading scriptures, yet claiming facts by taking one line/page, and making judgements about it. The wise ones have found Truth in all of them, because the Truth is right there in all of us.

How can it not be in one of the best expressions of us? If you don’t have time to study, better stay away from it. If you want to comment, better study. Just imagine a 12 year old coming at Scientific Literature with 8th grader knowledge. A lot of things in his book were written to simplify it for that 12 year old, but that doesn’t mean its not true, or its not representing Truth.

This is not me saying I know it, but this is the pattern that I have unraveled within these books. I have recognized a few lines, and these are enough pointers for a bigger mystery.
Science is one of the best portals to Truth. If you want to negate religion and scriptures, accept Science as the only Truth. It will take you to your being faster than almost all of those who follow religion.

But, if you already are a skeptic, find your own boxes to put reasoning and your spirituality into. Find contradictions. Don’t open these boxes when you need them just to win arguments. Soon enough, they will start talking to you. You need to give ideas time to settle.

Law, order, society, rituals, traditions, ideas etc. There is bit of truth in all of that but someone will disagree to it all the time. Its an attempt to localize answer for easing our lives. So, understand most of it as that.

Just focus on finding something that is not localized; something that doesn’t change if I put you in Nepal or US or Japan. That will be a good pointer for finding ideas that are universal. That is one good anchor to walk the walk.

सत्य आज मरिसक्यो
जीवनलाई छाडेपछि
मृत्यु सत्य बनिसक्यो
सत्य खोज्न थालेपछि ।।

Haha, this is one of the funniest things about life. There is one simple truth that I can tell you as well. “To this day, everybody who has lived, has died, sooner or later.” Death is simply washing away of all there is. But even Buddha believed in reincarnation.
Finding escape in death is easy, but only if it sure could be an escape. Life is meant to be lived with such vigor and ecstasy knowing its going to come to an end eventually.
Buddhist monks draw a Mandala out of sand, putting in all the effort for weeks for it to look flawless, only to wipe it off after completing it. That is not silly. That is a practice that gets closer to life than anything else. Just because we know that its going to extinguish doesn’t mean we are stopped from creating beauty. We can create beauty with an understanding that it will perish.

When we create beauty with that idea, beauty stands by itself: glorious.
And the way to live life is like that beauty. Those who live like that smell like Truth more than all those who are seeking it. Contradiction all the way, baby.

गढिमाईको मन्दीरमा
मृत्यु नै त सत्य बन्यो
न्याय बन्यो धर्म बन्यो
सत्य सँधै एक्लो बन्यो ।

This will be my controversial take on this after studying this for some time. This is a thin moral line but I don’t mind walking it.
As long as you eat meat, its better if you eat it as offering to some force rather than eating it as is like an animal. Because that helps you understand and lower your ego better. At least, you are recognizing something bigger than you. Making it a festive in hopes to appease Goddess, not so much. FYI: Its not for the main deity that you think the sacrifice is for. Unless there is purity in your heart, much of it is a waste anyway.

And for those who realize, they don’t even have to do a Sattvic Yajna or a ritual offering flowers. There is only one true offering: offering of your ego (false identity).

For those who realize, there is no difference between eating meat/ not eating meat. I don’t want to expound or teach anything. If you have a Guru, do what he tells you to do. If you don’t, guide it with your own moral compass.

You become more sensitive when you don’t eat. It eases your meditation as well. Stopping just at this.

कतै मुस्कान लहरसँगै
कतै रगत खोलो बग्यो
आलो रगत चरुसँगै
सत्य यज्ञ भष्म बन्यो ।

Death is one simple truth that we all know. The reason why they put Tika of “Bhasma** on their forehead in some traditions of Hinduism relates to this idea beautifully. You need to adore death as your personal friend. There are so many sects in Hinduism and Buddhism that meditate on the cremation ground. Death is but natural for them. Those who see it see everything as indifferent from one another.

Yes, truth is in that “Bhasma**. I didn’t know it at the time. I know it now. And its much pure than the best of temples you visit where people pretend to be, but have no true compassion.

All ideas of morality are fake if you don’t have an internal moral compass.

त्यै भष्मको कालो टीका
धर्मको त प्रतिक बन्यो
सत्य अब जलिसक्यो
यो माटोलाई त्यागिसक्यो
विनाशतिर लम्काएर
संसारदेखि भागिसक्यो ।।

Yes, this is the world we live in. Find those who don’t pretend, who are raw. They might hurt you, they might pain you, but they will eventually lead you to truth. You shouldn’t put on for anyone for it hides your being a little. Little by little, you forget who you are. You will be despised, desolate for doing so, but that’s the path of Truth.

Truth is personal. You cannot show it to someone who has closed their eyes by their own will.

Just look at how Premanand Maharaj talks about his Bhakti. That is a smell most people can understand.

So, this is my conclusion. I have traveled far and wide within myself and the world to realize what I do today. I am raw here because you know that you can be, at least with yourself personally. It is the best weapon to tear through all illusions.

A decade ago, I felt desolate, alone in my room. No idea where I was going, yet with almost everything that the world usually fights for. I had most of these things they wished, but it was only baggage for me. I didn’t know who I was. The only time I felt home was when I was below the night sky, watching those stars. They made me feel like they were watching me, protecting me. I felt alone among all the people who knew me. And in that desolate moment, I couldn’t see any light of truth anywhere. That’s why I wrote that last verse.

But today, I know that its almost everywhere for those who have the earnest eyes.

For those who don’t lie, even to themselves.

For those who are sensitive enough to look for it even in the remotest of places. There are stories of Sufi saints living as Butchers, so open your eyes to the possibility.

Don’t lie to yourself, even as self-deprecating humor.

What you don’t know, don’t assume. Ask if you have to. Write your things down.

Be patient with answers. Some questions take years to get answered, some might get answered by next person you meet.

Always be listening heartily, not to answer, listen to listen.

Anchor yourselves in Truth and Truth alone. Sooner or later, you will find that what you are looking for.

Be empathetic, be brave.

Truth is not for cowards.

There is a reason why they used emblem of Lotus flower. If you don’t have courage to get yourselves dirty, you have no point asking for that Lotus.

When you have that fragrance, the world will be a little bit more beautiful.

So, Bloom amidst the mud surrounding you !!

item.title: Nineteen Eighty Four 1984
item.description:
When they sell you the idea of freedom by saying they have removed all laws.

The thing that he was about to do was to open a diary. This was not illegal (nothing was illegal, since there were no longer any laws), but if detected it was reasonably certain that it would be punished by death, or at least by twenty-five years in a forced-labour camp.

Same thing in different language and emphasizing the last part as if they contradict each other to make you a slave.
item.content:
When they sell you the idea of freedom by saying they have removed all laws.

The thing that he was about to do was to open a diary. This was not illegal (nothing was illegal, since there were no longer any laws), but if detected it was reasonably certain that it would be punished by death, or at least by twenty-five years in a forced-labour camp.

Same thing in different language and emphasizing the last part as if they contradict each other to make you a slave.

The horrible thing about the Two Minutes Hate was not that one was obliged to act a part, but that it was impossible to avoid joining in.

WAR IS PEACE FREEDOM IS SLAVERY IGNORANCE IS STRENGTH.

Everything is being watched so that they know us inside out.

Asleep or awake, working or eating, indoors or out of doors, in the bath or in bed – no escape. Nothing was your own except the few cubic centimetres inside your skull.

He was a lonely ghost uttering a truth that nobody would ever hear. But so long as he uttered it, in some obscure way the continuity was not broken. It was not by making yourself heard but by staying sane that you carried on the human heritage.

Tragedy, he perceived, belonged to the ancient time, to a time when there was still privacy, love and friendship, and when the members of a family stood by one another without needing to know the reason.

Repeat the lie a thousand times and it becomes truth.

But where did that knowledge exist? Only in his own consciousness, which in any case must soon be annihilated. And if all others accepted the lie which the Party imposed – if all records told the same tale – then the lie passed into history and became truth.

Who do you trust? Where is the information? Who knows? What is the chance that it was said as it happened?

The past, he reflected, had not merely been altered, it had been actually destroyed. For how could you establish even the most obvious fact when there existed no record outside your own memory?

They will rewrite the narratives. Play the events with their own context. Extend minimal story to cover all of it.

Day by day and almost minute by minute the past was brought up to date. In this way every prediction made by the Party could be shown by documentary evidence to have been correct; nor was any item of news, or any expression of opinion, which conflicted with the needs of the moment, ever allowed to remain on record. All history was a palimpsest, scraped clean and re-inscribed exactly as often as was necessary.

The one that started without laws creates new types of crimes to make sure that there is unquestioned subservience to the authority.

Any case, to wear an improper expression on your face (to look incredulous when a victory was announced, for example) was itself a punishable offence. There was even a word for it in Newspeak: facecrime, it was called. The sexual act, successfully performed, was rebellion. Desire was thoughtcrime.

Until they become conscious they will never rebel, and until after they have rebelled they cannot become conscious.

Tie them in small problems and they will forget the big ones.

And even when they became discontented, as they sometimes did, their discontent led nowhere, because, being without general ideas, they could only focus it on petty specific grievances. The larger evils invariably escaped their notice.

Everything faded into mist. The past was erased, the erasure was forgotten, the lie became truth.

Freedom is the freedom to say that two plus two make four. If that is granted, all else follows.

How to use people by tapping and restricting on their primary instincts and desires by making it big offensive crime.

What was more important was that sexual privation induced hysteria, which was desirable because it could be transformed into war-fever and leader-worship.

Now, when slavery becomes a habit, its like drawing for air when one suffocates. Don’t have to hink and runs autonomously.

To hang on from day to day and from week to week, spinning out a present that had no future, seemed an unconquerable instinct, just as one’s lungs will always draw the next breath so long as there is air available.

The ones who are easy to use are the ones who are incapable of grasping the full picture.

In a way, the world-view of the Party imposed itself most successfully on people incapable of understanding it. They could be made to accept the most flagrant violations of reality, because they never fully grasped the enormity of what was demanded of them, and were not sufficiently interested in public events to notice what was happening.

In the long run, a hierarchical society was only possible on a basis of poverty and ignorance.

Doublethink means the power of holding two contradictory beliefs in one’s mind simultaneously, and accepting both of them.

If one is to rule, and to continue ruling, one must be able to dislocate the sense of reality. For the secret of rulership is to combine a belief in one’s own infallibility with the power to learn from past mistakes.

Being in a minority, even a minority of one, did not make you mad. There was truth and there was untruth, and if you clung to the truth even against the whole world, you were not mad.

It was more natural to exist from moment to moment, accepting another ten minutes’ life even with the certainty that there was torture at the end of it.

‘Have you ever seen those bones, Winston? Of course not. Nineteenth-century biologists invented them. Before man there was nothing. After man, if he could come to an end, there would be nothing. Outside man there is nothing.’

To die hating them, that was freedom.

Never use a metaphor, simile or other figure of speech which you are used to seeing in print. ii. Never use a long word where a short one will do. iii. If it is possible to cut a word out, always cut it out. iv. Never use the passive where you can use the active. v. Never use a foreign phrase, a scientific word or a jargon word if you can think of an everyday English equivalent. vi. Break any of these rules sooner than say anything outright barbarous.

Kindle highlights (2020)

  • loc 800 - sentimental songs which were composed entirely by mechanical means on a special kind of kaleidoscope known as a versificator.

  • loc 929 - In the end we shall make thoughtcrime literally impossible, because there will be no words in which to express it

  • loc 1041 - Why should one feel it to be intolerable unless one had some kind of ancestral memory that things had once been different?

  • loc 1073 - any case, to wear an improper expression on your face (to look incredulous when a victory was announced, for example) was itself a punishable offence. There was even a word for it in Newspeak: facecrime, it was called.

  • loc 1073 - In any case, to wear an improper expression on your face (to look incredulous when a victory was announced, for example) was itself a punishable offence. There was even a word for it in Newspeak: facecrime, it was called.

  • loc 1156 - The sexual act, successfully performed, was rebellion. Desire was thoughtcrime.

  • loc 1400 - The Lottery, with its weekly pay-out of enormous prizes, was the one public event to which the proles paid serious attention. It was probable that there were some millions of proles for whom the Lottery was the principal if not the only reason for remaining alive.

  • loc 2150 - The words of these songs were composed without any human intervention whatever on an instrument known as a versificator. But the woman sang so tunefully as to turn the dreadful rubbish into an almost pleasant sound.

  • loc 2385 - ‘Who cares?’ she said impatiently. ‘It’s always one bloody war after another, and one knows the news is all lies anyway.’

  • loc 2993 - War prisoners apart, the average citizen of Oceania never sets eyes on a citizen of either Eurasia or Eastasia, and he is forbidden the knowledge of foreign languages. If he were allowed contact with foreigners he would discover that they are creatures similar to himself and that most of what he has been told about them is lies.

  • loc 3104 - as early as the beginning of the twentieth century, human equality had become technically possible. It was still true that men were not equal in their native talents and that functions had to be specialised in ways that favoured some individuals against others; but there was no longer any real need for class distinctions or for large differences of wealth. In earlier ages, class distinctions had been not only inevitable but desirable. Inequality was the price of civilisation. With the development of machine production, however, the case was altered. Even if it was still necessary for human beings to do different kinds of work, it was no longer necessary for them to live at different social or economic levels.

  • loc 3130 - Even the Catholic Church of the Middle Ages was tolerant by modern standards.

  • loc 3972 - The German Nazis and the Russian Communists came very close to us in their methods, but they never had the courage to recognise their own motives. They pretended, perhaps they even believed, that they had seized power unwillingly and for a limited time, and that just round the corner there lay a paradise where human beings would be free and equal. We are not like that.

  • loc 3996 - You must get rid of those nineteenth-century ideas about the laws of Nature. We make the laws of Nature.’

  • loc 5050 - i. Never use a metaphor, simile or other figure of speech which you are used to seeing in print. ii. Never use a long word where a short one will do. iii. If it is possible to cut a word out, always cut it out. iv. Never use the passive where you can use the active. v. Never use a foreign phrase, a scientific word or a jargon word if you can think of an everyday English equivalent. vi. Break any of these rules sooner than say anything outright barbarous.

item.title: Smiling like a madman
item.description:
First I was innocent,
I asked for an identity,
The world pushed me down and pained me.
I talked to the world about this pain,
And the world mocked me.


I felt alone in this fight,
I wanted to run away.
But, she didn't let me.
She made me break into a thousand pieces,
But always took great care that none was lost.
And when I gave up,
She made me work on myself.
And That's how I recollected myself to be wholler than the whole.


-------------------------------xx-------------------------------


Second I was in limelight,
I asked for strength,
Then the eyes of the world fixated at me pained me.
Their dreams, their expectations,
Them trying to fulfill their dreams through me.
I again talked to the world about the burden of expectations,
And the world really didn't care.

I felt alone again in this fight,
I wanted to run away.
But, she didn't let me.
She made me take even more burden until I broke again,
Yet she took great care again that none was lost.
And when I gave up,
She made me work on myself.
And That's how I recollected myself to be wholler than the whole again.


-------------------------------xx-------------------------------


Third, I was now strong enough to take any burden.
I asked for truth,
I started wandering here and there in search of truth,
The words from thousand masters buzzed like a bomb inside my head.
But by now, I knew the world never listened.
So I chose a few I was hoping would listen without judgement,
Tried telling them about the never ending search,
Yet they too didn’t get much.

I asked for an identity,
The world pushed me down and pained me.
I talked to the world about this pain,
And the world mocked me.


I felt alone in this fight,

But, she didn't let me.

But always took great care that none was lost.
And when I gave up,
She made me work on myself.
And That's how I recollected myself to be wholler than the whole.


-------------------------------xx-------------------------------


Second I was in limelight,
I asked for strength,
Then the eyes of the world fixated at me pained me.
Their dreams, their expectations,
Them trying to fulfill their dreams through me.
I again talked to the world about the burden of expectations,
And the world really didn't care.

I felt alone again in this fight,
I wanted to run away.
But, she didn't let me.
She made me take even more burden until I broke again,
Yet she took great care again that none was lost.
And when I gave up,
She made me work on myself.
And That's how I recollected myself to be wholler than the whole again.


-------------------------------xx-------------------------------


Third, I was now strong enough to take any burden.
I asked for truth,
I started wandering here and there in search of truth,
The words from thousand masters buzzed like a bomb inside my head.
But by now, I knew the world never listened.
So I chose a few I was hoping would listen without judgement,
Tried telling them about the never ending search,
Yet they too didn’t get much.



I was feeling utterly alone by then,
I wanted to run away.
But, she didn't let me.
I had to sit there with thousand petals opening inside me,
Yet not even an eye to appreciate.
I wanted to help those few to make it bloom in them,
Yet each one had their own doubts.


The petals bloomed,
The petals faded,
And they fell back to the ground.
Forgetting the fact that it is the nature of petals to fall off,
I started crying seeing all those petals within withering away,
Yet she took great care to collect them all for me.
And when I gave up crying,
She held my hand,
She reached out to me with the incense she prepared from those flowers,
And That’s how I recollected myself to be wholler than the whole again.



-------------------------------xx-------------------------------


Fourth, I realized myself and my relationship with her.
Through her eyes,
I realized the world too was her all along.
Now, I was no longer bashing my head,
Neither was I trying to make the world understand me.
I was happy with the fragrance she left me with.


One day, I realized she had been with me the whole time,
And then, I no longer needed to run away.
I no longer needed to say anything to the world,
Or hear back something from there.
I no longer was bashing my head.
I was just there lost in the fragrance of the flowers,
And she came.
She asked me to not get lost in that fragrance,
And gave me keys to her garden itself.


Now, I sit there smiling like a madman. ☺️

item.title: Dream of Himalayan Yogis
item.description:
The Dream of Liberation: From Fear to Truth

The wise ones teach that the universe was born from the desire of The One—not out of pity, not to cause pain, but from a longing to multiply and know itself.

As the Chhandogya Upanishad (6.2.1) declares,

“sadeva somyedamagra āsīdekamevādvitīyam

taddhaika āhurasadevedamagra

āsīdekamevādvitīyaṃ tasmādasataḥ sajjāyata”

—“Somya, before this world was manifest there was only existence, one without a second. On this subject, some maintain that before this world was manifest there was only non-existence, one without a second. Out of that non-existence, existence emerged.”
item.content:
The Dream of Liberation: From Fear to Truth

The wise ones teach that the universe was born from the desire of The One—not out of pity, not to cause pain, but from a longing to multiply and know itself.

As the Chhandogya Upanishad (6.2.1) declares,

“sadeva somyedamagra āsīdekamevādvitīyam

taddhaika āhurasadevedamagra

āsīdekamevādvitīyaṃ tasmādasataḥ sajjāyata”

—“Somya, before this world was manifest there was only existence, one without a second. On this subject, some maintain that before this world was manifest there was only non-existence, one without a second. Out of that non-existence, existence emerged.”

Similarly, the Aitareya Upanishad (1.1.1) states,

“om atma va idameka evagra asit nanyat kincana misat sa iksata lokannu srija iti ”

—“OM ! In the beginning this was but the absolute Self alone . There was nothing else whatsoever that winked . It thought , " Let Me create the worlds ." ”

Again, Brihadharanyak Upanishad (1.4.2) says,

“Sa va na iva reme,tasmād ekākī na ramate;

sa dvitīya ma icchat”

—“The One didn’t enjoy being solitary. Therefore, the one desired to be two.

From this primal desire, consciousness split, and the universe exploded into multiplicity. But with this division came pain and suffering, born from the loss of divinity. No longer The One, we became bottles of consciousness—confused, searching, unaware of our origin or destination. What was meant to be a game of enjoyment isn’t enjoyment anymore. Yet, as the sages remind us, it’s alright to be confused. The journey back to truth begins with patience. Shakti upasaks and Sufi saints are the prime examples of who can enjoy this duality like no one else. If you understand its a game you chose to play, then it can be fun and exciting for you. But that’s a whole another story for another day. Lets just focus on “Dream of Liberation” for now.

And in that same Brihadaranyak Upanishad, (1.4.1) there is this quote just above this one that goes like this:

sa abibhet

tasmād ekākī bibheti;

sa ha ayam īkṣāṃ cakre,

yat mad anyan nāsti,

kaṣma annu bibhema īti,

tata evāsya bhayaṃ vīyāya,

kasma addhyabheṣyat

dvitīyādvai bhayaṃ bhavati

which means

“It was alone and became fearful. Reflecting, it thought, ‘Since there is nothing else but me, what is there to fear?’ Thus, its fear vanished. For fear arises only from the presence of another.”

I hope this clarifies fear, desire and truth as said by the wise ones.

I’ve never met a Himalayan Yogi my entire life. Yet, their idea reached me through multiple books and biographies of such saints. Their vision, I believe, is Spiritual Liberation —a return to unity, to the unconditioned state of being. But there’s a closer dream, a stepping stone: liberation from fear. I’d read it somewhere that’s their immediate dream. So, I am here to contribute to that dream. This is where my story begins, and where I hope to make a difference.

Buddha’s Truth: Life is Suffering

Lets understand fear and suffering with another lens. A lens that’s so sharp and astute. None other than Buddha and his teachings.

When the Buddha attained enlightenment, his first words captured the essence of existence:

“Anekajāti samsāram, Sandhāvissam anibbisam, Gahakārakam gavesanto, Dukkhā jāti punappunam”—“Through many a birth in samsara, have I wandered in vain, seeking the builder of this house of life. Repeated birth is indeed suffering.”

He saw the house-builder—the cycle of craving—and declared,

“Gahakāraka dittho si, Puna gehaṁ na kāhasi”—“O house-builder, you are seen. You will not build this house again.”

His mind reached the unconditioned, free from desire.

Buddha, a Himalayan Yogi in spirit, revealed the Four Noble Truths, the first being: Life is suffering. Through paths like Hinayana, Mahayana, and Vajrayana, he offered ways to transcend this suffering. Today, Tibetan monks in the Himalayan foothills practice his teachings, meditating in dark caves for years, seeking liberation.

Upon first glance, Buddha’s view seems to contradict the idea of desire. But if you have studied Buddhism in little more depth, then you know what created the house in the first place. And that Buddha is indeed talking about “Desire” that was building the house again and again. Like the wise quote, “Truth is One but the explanations are many.”

From them, we inherited tools like meditation and yoga—ancient practices, nearly 2,000 years old, designed not to ease our worldly stress but to cut through the illusion of existence and attain nirvana, enlightenment, unity.

Yet, modern practitioners often misunderstand these tools. Yoga’s Eightfold Path—Yama, Niyama, Asana, Pranayama, Pratyahara, Dharana, Dhyana, and Samadhi—is rarely followed in its entirety. Even yoga teachers struggle to grasp its depth. Meditation, too, is often reduced to a quick fix for daily stress, far from its original purpose. This realization drove me to create something new, rooted in the wisdom of the past but tailored to our present needs. I’m no teacher, but as a keen student, I’ve looked deeper than most. Through eight years of meditation, study of Hinduism, Buddhism, stories of Sufi saints, and even Egyptian history, I’ve glimpsed the essence of the Yogis’ dream.

My Journey: The Truth That Transforms

My transformation began with Vipassana, the meditation technique taught by the Buddha. I had read many scriptures, but I had zero experience of truth.

Two 10-day silent retreats revealed truths that had been invisible, lurking right before my eyes. Then, in a single moment, reality struck me with undeniable force, like lightning, shattering my illusions.

Years later, I realized it wasn’t the silence or the process that transformed me — it was the truth staring me down, impossible to ignore. I fought so hard that when it broke me, the light entered.

Words from scriptures and wise ones became more clearer as I continued meditating.

I’ve seen others attend Vipassana retreats, some even 20 times, yet miss the fundamental lesson. I’ve met those who can quote scriptures fluently but never grasp their essence. My fortune lies in recognizing what truly changed me: not a technique, but the raw encounter with my personal truth. And I want that to happen with you too.

The Vision: An App to Face Fear

This insight inspired me to create an app—not for liberation or enlightenment, but for a more immediate goal: to help you face your undeniable truth and liberate yourself from fear. Fear binds us, just as it bound our cave-dwelling ancestors. Despite humanity’s progress—our trust in one another, our interconnected lives sustained by thousands across the globe—we still fear the world. We eat food we don’t grow, wear clothes we don’t make, yet tremble with the same primal anxieties.

This app is a tool to clean your mirror, to reflect your truth clearly. It’s meant to be used and then discarded, like a ladder climbed and left behind. It won’t grant spiritual liberation, but it will take you to the first step: a world where fear no longer drives you. Generations have survived wars, brutality, and chaos, yet we’ve grown together, trusted, and thrived. This app will remind you of that resilience, showing you a world there’s not much to fear. Most of your anxieties comes from your caveman survival instinct deeply coded onto your genes.

Unlocking Infinite Potential

You sit atop infinite potential, bound only by fear. My mission is to help you unlock it. This journey may take years, even decades, but with true effort, you’ll be able to find your personal truth. You will finally live like royalty—free to meditate, to create, to arrive at the world awaiting you. Until your mirror is clean, you cannot comprehend what lies ahead.

The Himalayan Yogis dreamed of spiritual liberation, but their closer dream—freedom from fear—is within our reach. This app is my offering to that vision, a bridge to a fearless world. Let’s eliminate fear first. Then, together, we’ll see what comes next.

I had the idea almost two years ago. I am sorry for taking this long to build this. Finally as AI got better, it helped my development path quiet a lot. This is not a sales pitch because I don’t expect anything from you except that you someday arrive at that place where I arrived some years ago.

No data collection, no ads, no money to pay.

Locked to only you so that you can record deepest darkest thoughts without worrying a bit. Just use it so that one day you can throw it away. I might add feature to share your stories to one another for moral boost someday. Until then, its not even connecting to the internet.

Only thing that it requires is your attention to your life: observing the patterns of your mind until you’re free from it.

This is my personal motivation and my dream behind creating this project.

More tools will come at https://maitreyatools.com.

item.title: The Joy of Abstraction
item.description:
Representation and Symbols

  • If we’re talking about a one-element set we often declare the single element to be an asterisk ∗ to remind ourselves that it has no meaning. The resulting one-element set is then written {∗}.

Chapter 1 and 2

  • Rigorous logic being problematic is starting point for category theory as well.
  • “Abstraction is the process of deciding on some details to ignore in order to ensure that our logic does work perfectly.” e.g. Think of the difference between map and territories in a way. Though maps seem very different, having different maps helps us understand territory better using connections. And same kind of relationships can be translated and reused.
  • All about zooming in and out.
  • Category Theory always needs context first. Similar to BR The Courage of Being Disliked where it says all problems are interpersonal problems. Unless there are more than one node a.k.a a relationship, there is no problem at all.
  • “We will see that category theory is a framework that achieves a remarkable trade-off between good behavior and expressive possibilities. If a framework demands too much good behavior then expressivity is limited, as in a totalitarian state with very strict laws. On the other hand if there are too few demands, then there is great potential for expressivity, but also for chaos and anarchy. Category theory achieves a productive balance between those, in the way it specifies what type of relationship it is going to study.”
  • Not limited to numbers. Not limited to equations. Not limited as long as “sameness” can be defined properly.
  • Doesn’t look into a node. Only role it plays in context.
  • Different contexts, same relationships even results to different understanding, different conclusions.
  • If category theory is theory of mathematics, then higher dimensional category theory is theory of categories.
  • Logic + Abstraction
  • “I would say that philosophy uses logic, but applies it to real questions about life experiences. Art uses abstraction, but does not primarily build on its abstractions by logic. Math uses logic and abstraction together. It uses logic to build rigorous arguments, and uses abstraction to ensure that we are working in a world where logic can be made rigorous.”
  • Abstraction in definition is very close to trying for generalization in AI. Trying to find good abstraction that just covers essentials between nodes without having everything.
  • Stripping out the details to reveal a relationship sturcture is what category theory is all about.
  • Moral abstractions require us to make sure we are using the same type of relationship between nodes, else the idea of sameness cannot be applied.
  • The goal isn’t to find most abstract possible level. Goal is to find a good enough abstraction in order to solve a problem.
  • Different context, different truths.
  • By stripping the details, we can always take everything to the same level but that might not be what we need. Too much details is bad, so is too much abstraction. Rather than even be fixed at certain level, we can move between different levels and see a good picture about our problem at hand.
  • Addition and multiplication:
    • Both are binary operations.
    • Both are Associative
    • Both are Commutative
    • Addition is reversible by subtraction while multiplication is not always reversible by division.

Process of moving between levels of abstraction :

  1. See an analogy between some different things (a.k.a defining the first level)
  2. Specify what we are regarding as causing the analogy (a.k.a. defining the direction from this first level)
  3. Regard that thing as a new, more abstract, concept in its own right(a.k.a. taking the direction and specifying this second level)
  4. Be comfortable with new abstract concepts without thinking that they are abstract (a.k.a. understanding this second level in its own right as if first level didn’t exist)
  5. See analogy between some of these new concepts (a.k.a. trying to find new direction from this level)
  6. Iterate (a.k.a loop )

Example

  1. Start with statement " If we add two numbers, the order we put them in doesn’t matter. " [ First level ]
  2. By converting them to numbers, “Given any numbers a and b, a+b = b+a” [ Defining the direction: From letters to numbers a,b ]
  3. Now this process of a and b to a+b or b+a is a concept called addition. [ Point 3 and 4 together ]
  4. Process that takes two numbers and produces a number a . b [ Taking a new direction of abstraction from addition ]
  5. Now from that we can take it in direction of multiplication [ a * b = c which is multiplication ]

In conclusion, the top level becomes abstract binary operation. This is starting point to so many branches of mathematics being applied starting from categorical principles.
item.content:
Representation and Symbols

  • If we’re talking about a one-element set we often declare the single element to be an asterisk ∗ to remind ourselves that it has no meaning. The resulting one-element set is then written {∗}.

Chapter 1 and 2

  • Rigorous logic being problematic is starting point for category theory as well.
  • “Abstraction is the process of deciding on some details to ignore in order to ensure that our logic does work perfectly.” e.g. Think of the difference between map and territories in a way. Though maps seem very different, having different maps helps us understand territory better using connections. And same kind of relationships can be translated and reused.
  • All about zooming in and out.
  • Category Theory always needs context first. Similar to BR The Courage of Being Disliked where it says all problems are interpersonal problems. Unless there are more than one node a.k.a a relationship, there is no problem at all.
  • “We will see that category theory is a framework that achieves a remarkable trade-off between good behavior and expressive possibilities. If a framework demands too much good behavior then expressivity is limited, as in a totalitarian state with very strict laws. On the other hand if there are too few demands, then there is great potential for expressivity, but also for chaos and anarchy. Category theory achieves a productive balance between those, in the way it specifies what type of relationship it is going to study.”
  • Not limited to numbers. Not limited to equations. Not limited as long as “sameness” can be defined properly.
  • Doesn’t look into a node. Only role it plays in context.
  • Different contexts, same relationships even results to different understanding, different conclusions.
  • If category theory is theory of mathematics, then higher dimensional category theory is theory of categories.
  • Logic + Abstraction
  • “I would say that philosophy uses logic, but applies it to real questions about life experiences. Art uses abstraction, but does not primarily build on its abstractions by logic. Math uses logic and abstraction together. It uses logic to build rigorous arguments, and uses abstraction to ensure that we are working in a world where logic can be made rigorous.”
  • Abstraction in definition is very close to trying for generalization in AI. Trying to find good abstraction that just covers essentials between nodes without having everything.
  • Stripping out the details to reveal a relationship sturcture is what category theory is all about.
  • Moral abstractions require us to make sure we are using the same type of relationship between nodes, else the idea of sameness cannot be applied.
  • The goal isn’t to find most abstract possible level. Goal is to find a good enough abstraction in order to solve a problem.
  • Different context, different truths.
  • By stripping the details, we can always take everything to the same level but that might not be what we need. Too much details is bad, so is too much abstraction. Rather than even be fixed at certain level, we can move between different levels and see a good picture about our problem at hand.
  • Addition and multiplication:
    • Both are binary operations.
    • Both are Associative
    • Both are Commutative
    • Addition is reversible by subtraction while multiplication is not always reversible by division.

Process of moving between levels of abstraction :

  1. See an analogy between some different things (a.k.a defining the first level)
  2. Specify what we are regarding as causing the analogy (a.k.a. defining the direction from this first level)
  3. Regard that thing as a new, more abstract, concept in its own right(a.k.a. taking the direction and specifying this second level)
  4. Be comfortable with new abstract concepts without thinking that they are abstract (a.k.a. understanding this second level in its own right as if first level didn’t exist)
  5. See analogy between some of these new concepts (a.k.a. trying to find new direction from this level)
  6. Iterate (a.k.a loop )

Example

  1. Start with statement " If we add two numbers, the order we put them in doesn’t matter. " [ First level ]
  2. By converting them to numbers, “Given any numbers a and b, a+b = b+a” [ Defining the direction: From letters to numbers a,b ]
  3. Now this process of a and b to a+b or b+a is a concept called addition. [ Point 3 and 4 together ]
  4. Process that takes two numbers and produces a number a . b [ Taking a new direction of abstraction from addition ]
  5. Now from that we can take it in direction of multiplication [ a * b = c which is multiplication ]

In conclusion, the top level becomes abstract binary operation. This is starting point to so many branches of mathematics being applied starting from categorical principles.

Simple example of abstracting to binary operation:

More complex example

Chapter 3 Patterns

  • Patterns are aesthetic and functional.
    • e.g. Repetitive tiles
    • base 10 numbers
  • Category theory is all about patterns a.k.a the underlying structure
  • When you analyse patterns deeply, we can go layres deep to find patterns within patterns as well.
  • Difference of levels: mother-daughter relation between generations becomes a different relation when skipped a level: grandmother-granddaughter
  • Visual patterns help derive analogy, abstraction of the structure of those patterns help reason and do more complex operations with those analogies.
    • We should be able to see simple patterns visually and blow them to understand high level patterns that are complicated to visualize.

Example of using category theory pattern matching in real life conflict

Disagreement usually arises in two forms if we follow category theory ardently. Suppose A and B are two ideas, and X and Y are abstract levels of categories:

  1. Someone sees principle W at work which is behind A, so A and B are not analogous.
  2. They see another general principle Y that they think first person is invoking. And that makes some other C analogous. Then they object to that.

Chapter 4 Context

  • In category theory, truth depends on context.
  • Even things we generally assume as true will be questioned using a different context. So, we need to be very flexible with changing contexts.

Distance

  • When we take distance and try to abstract it to a circle on a line grid, we have to say we move by a fixed distance on the grid. Then that abstraction of our understanding of distance on a grid with limitation of fixed distance from a center point gets us this shape.
  • So, it tells us that we can create so many different types of distances based on the restrictions or rules. So, the context matters for truth.

Different context of numbers we use in daily lives

  • 2 hours after 11 isn’t 13 in a 12-hour clock. It’s 1. It doesn’t need to be just about 12. We literally can have n-hour clocks.
  • Rotating something by 90 degrees four times makes it back to original. a.k.a 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 0
  • Mixing paint 1 + 1 = 1

Chapter 5 Relationships

  • So context is defined by relationships or vice versa.
    • If we relate fruits by color, we get a different context than when we relate fruits by taste.
  • Distance is a type of relationship but depending on whether its streets, airspace, it can be totally different. So, context matters.
  • Zero world: Multiple items can look as if they are same in certain context but when we take them somewhere else, they might start looking different.

Example : Family Relationship

Now, same abstraction can be used with ease to other contexts as well.

Example of mapping the relationship

Mapping relation for rotating a square.

Arithmetic Relationship

Similar to squares, we have the relationship but this table is not finite. So, we don’t even need to have full table to properly understand the pattern as a result of the relationship.

Quadrilaterals

By releasing certain conditions or applying certain conditions, we get to more general cases.

When we draw the same composition like a venn diagram, it looks like this:

But still we have problems:

  • All rhombuses are kites, so the kite circle needs to contain the entire rhombus circle.
  • A kite that is not a rhombus is also not a parallelogram or a trapezoid, so the kite circle needs to stick out into the random quadrilateral part without overlapping the parallelogram or trapezoid circles.

Lattices of factors

We see a similar type of relationship structure. Also by drawing such a structure, we can go into many more details like: what does each face of cube represent? What are edges telling us? Can we know the shape before drawing it based on prime factors it can have etc. etc.

Inferring patterns from structure

e.g. The square faces tell us things like the fact that multiplying by 2 and then 3 is the same as multiplying by 3 and then 2, i.e. that multiplication is commutative.

The dimension of the shape can give us how many prime factors it has. If its a 2D shape, it only has two prime factors. If its 3d, it has 3 prime factors.

Inferring other types of relationships from this one

We can clearly see that same structure arises in subset relationship.

And not just maths, anywhere :

Now, what goes higher in hierarchy can be different e.g. In lattice of factors, 6 goes higher than 7 because its not prime and has two prime factors. So, we need to understand what we are defining by levels. Our levels can have meaning, hierarchy or not. Most conflict happen because we don’t agree on level of abstractions.

Chapter 6 Formalism

  • Mathematical notation is used for efficiency and abstraction. It becomes so complicated if we had to do all our maths using English language.
  • Concise notation to make complex entities simpler which is abstraction at its core.
    • e.g. 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 replaced by 3 x 4
  • Exponential growth vs linear growth when we talk in that terms, maths and science people immediately know what is growing faster.

Metric Spaces

  • Different types of distances are called “metrics”.
  • Some criterion for distances are:
    • Distance is a number
    • Distance isn’t negative
    • Distance from same point to same point should be zero. We say d(A, B) = 0 if and only if A = B.
    • Symmetry d(A, B) = d(B, A)
    • Detours [ Triangle Inequality ] If you stop off somewhere along the way it should not make your distance any less. At best it won’t change the distance, but it might well make the journey longer. d(A, X) + d(X, B) >= d(A, B)
  • So, these criterion define distance. By releasing certain criterion, we might get different examples.

Basic Logic

Logic is based on logical implication. A > B A if B written as B < A A only if B written as A => B

Modular Arithmetic (Very interesting example indeed )

How do we say “is a multiple of 6” using formal language

Start by using another random letter “k” to represent whole number, so multiple of 6 is 6k. However, we used an extra letter. 6k = m

So, instead of using that notation, mathematicians came up with this notation: 6 | m which means “6 divides m” or “6 goes into m” which is saying the same thing “multiple of 6” but other way around.

So, when we talk about modulo “a and b occupy the same position” we say “a-b| 6” for modulo arithmetic table. Then mathematicians said “congruent modulo 6” or “congruent mod 6” to say this thing for short. In notation form, a ≡ b (mod 6)

Now using the same notation, we write “integers modulo 6” as \(\mathbb{Z}_{6}\).

\(a \in \mathbb{Z}\) is shorthand for “a is an element of \(\mathbb{Z}\).

Example definition

  • Let \(a, b \in \mathbb{Z}\) Then \(a \equiv b (mod 6)\) if and only if 6|b-a.

Why didn’t we write => instead of “if and only if” because we are trying to define the thing on the left using thing on the right. Not trying to create equivalence.

  • Let \(n \in \mathbb{Z}_{+}\) and \(a,b \in \mathbb{Z}\). Then \(a \equiv b\) (mod n) iff \(n | b -a\).

Also try to think of informal proof before trying to prove it formally and that will make most things easier.

Chapter 7 Equivalence Relations

  • Category theory if allowed to study with any kind of relationship can get really chaotic. So, mildest conditions for type of relationship is defined.
  • Equality without a good condition is hard. So, reasons for equality need to be defined.
  • Relations really can be abstract a RELN b.
  • Reflexivity involves only one object at a time, Symmetry involves two, Transitivity involves three. But it doesn’t mean these three or two need to be distinct objects.

Reflexivity

  • A relation is called reflexive if it sees everything related to itself. i.e. every object satisfies an abstract relation a RELN a. This is property of relation, not of object/node.

Asking questions about reflexivity of relations

Proving via counter example

Symmetry

  • If its same both way around.
  • If definition says a RELN b => b RELN a, then if we switch the roles of a and b we get, b RELN a => a RELN b. so, combining those we get: a RELN b <=> b RELN a.
  • So, statements are logically equivalent. a RELN b and b RELN a.

Example where its symmetric

Example where its not symmetric

Transitivity

The case of less than relation which was neither symmetric nor reflexive is at least transitive.

Equivalence Relation

  • If a relation RELN on a set S is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

The relation itself depends on the kind of surface we are dealing with. If its a globe, how do we say what’s east. So, due to such reasons we need to restrict our context first.

  • Equivalence relations are too well behaved that they are not interesting. So, we relax our conditions.

Chapter 8 Categories

  • Based on the equivalence relation and relaxing of it, we are ready to define category. It contains three parts:
    • Data
    • Structure
    • Properties

Data

  • Objects can be anything
  • world “S” of objects we are going to consider category \(\mathcr{C}\)
  • Relationships can be “less than”, “equals” etc. We call them Morphisms or Arrows.
  • We really aren’t asking whether they are equal in category. We are asking “in what ways are these objects related?”
  • No limit to number of arrows that can go from one object to other.
  • When we focus on set of objects we write collection of arrows as \(\mathcr{C}(a,b)\). Or we can write in terms of Homsets in Category Theory homc(a,b). Set of these morphisms is called homset.

Structure

  • We don’t go with stricter conditions of equivalence like last time. We relax conditions.
  • For any object a, there must at least be an arrow to itself called identity.
  • Composition. For every relation that goes from a to b and b to c there will be a composed arrow that goes from a to c.
    • They don’t have to be transitive or true/false. We just need to ensure that a morphism exists.
    • Arrows have to be composable. Target of first one must match the source of second and so on.

Properties

  • One for identity
  • One for composing more than two arrows
  • Also called axioms. These are the ones governing structure.

Identity Morphism

  • Does not do anything. Starts at the object and returns the object.
    • e.g. 0 is the identity for addition on real numbers.
  • So, here : f ˆ 1a = f = 1b ˆ f

Composition Morphism

This is how we compose these arrows. This is associativity. h ˆ ( g ˆ f ) = (h ˆ g) ˆ f

Formal definition

A category C consists of:

  • Data
    • Objects: a collection obC of objects
    • Arrows: for objects a, b ∈ obC, a collection C(a, b) of arrows a -> b
  • Structure
    • Identities: for any object a ∈ obC an identity arrow a -1a-> a
    • Composition: for any arrows a -f-> b -g-> c, where a,b,c are nodes and f,g are relations. a composite arrow a -g◦f-> c
  • Properties
    • Unit laws: for any arrow a -f-> b, f ◦ 1a = f = 1b ◦ f
    • Associativity: for any arrows a -f-> b -g-> c -h-> d, (h ◦ g) ◦ f = h ◦ (g ◦ f)
  • Arrows are also called morphisms, and the composite g ◦ f is also written gf .

We loosened equivalence to this. And for equality, we will look at invertibility which is more subtle notion of sameness in categories so that they are more useful to build everything.

Sizes

  • Category where objects and morphisms form a set is called small.
  • Category where each individual collection C(a,b) is a set, then its called locally small. In this case, they might form a collection, not a set.

Geometry of associativity

This gets translated into a full pyramid like 3d image.

Drawing a category

  • Usually don’t draw identity arrows. Assumed to exist there.
  • Omit arrows whose existence can be deduced from composition.
  • Physical positioning doesn’t affect structure.

Chapter 9 Basic Maths

  • Trivial symmetry : A symmetry that might not be considered useful in real life. e.g. rotation by 0 degrees for a square is its identity arrow which is a trivial symmetry.
  • For a category we draw from factors, we started by pointing arrows from prime factors toward the number. If we reverse the arrows, it still contains same information as the last category. Such a category where arrows are reversed, is called a Dual Category.

Category Theory in Number system

  • Thinking of these numbers in terms of addition
  • objects : natural numbers
  • arrows : a -> b whenever a ≤ b
  • Every other number is related to itself and every other but since these can be derived from plain relation we can write it as: 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 …
  • We need a less than or equal to or greater than or equal to to satisfy the identity constraint. Now, we just know what dual here looks like as well.

Summing up equivalence relations

Chapter 10 Ordered Sets

Tosets

  • Totally ordered sets
  • Category in which for all objects a,b there is exactly one arrow between them.
  • Can’t have arrow both ways from a -> b and b -> a unless a = b in that case both arrows mean identity.
  • e.g. Category of natural numbers with relation a ≤ b is a totally ordered set according to the definition.

Examples of when its not toset

Two objects on the right don’t have morphism betwen them. Same for two objects on the left on second one. Two arrows from one object to another on the third one. Multiple arrows even though one object on the fourth one.

Non-categorical definition of ordered set

An ordered set is a set S equipped with a binary relation ≤ satisfying

  • reflexivity: a ≤ a for all a ∈ S
  • antisymmetry: if a ≤ b and b ≤ a then a = b
  • transitivity: if a ≤ b and b ≤ c then a ≤ c
  • trichotomy: for all a, b ∈ S , a ≤ b or b ≤ a

Now coming to categorical definition from this one

Reflexivity is a special case of trichotomy: if we put a = b in the definition of trichotomy we get “a ≤ a or a ≤ a”, which is reflexivity. It’s useful to state it as a condition though, because when we relax the conditions later we will need to specify it. In the categorical definition we don’t need the other conditions because:

  • Reflexivity comes from the category having identities.
  • Transitivity comes from composition in the category.
  • Antisymmetry and trichotomy both come from there being exactly one arrow between a and b: antisymmetry comes from there being at most one, and trichotomy from there being at least one.

Posets

  • Partially ordered sets
  • Relaxing the condition of tosets saying there can be at most one arrow between two objects, but possibly none.
  • The condition we need to drop is trichotomy, as we now want to allow pairs of objects that are not related either way round.

Non categorical definition of posets

A partially ordered set or poset is a set S equipped with a relation ≤ satisfying:

  • reflexivity: a ≤ a for all a ∈ S
  • antisymmetry: if a ≤ b and b ≤ a then a = b
  • transitivity: if a ≤ b and b ≤ c then a ≤ c.

Chapter 11 Small mathematical structures

  • For a category to be defined, we can just draw its structure and call it an abstract category.
  • A set is a category with no arrows between objects, just the identity arrow. Such a category is called Discrete category. Also we call identity arrows “trivial”, so discrete category can be thought of as one that has no non-trivial arrows.

Monoids

Suppose every time we compose that loop with itself we get a new arrow. In that case this category has only one object but infinitely many arrows. If we call the basic arrow f then:

  • There is also f ◦ f which we might write as f2.
  • Then there is f ◦ f ◦ f which we might write as f3.
  • In fact there’s fn for every n ∈ N.

Note it makes sense to include 0 in N here, with f0 = 1, the identity. So, even if its a loop, its not identity by default. We have multiple relations from itself to itself.

Example would be when natural numbers are not written as separate blobs but instead written as infinite loop relations like +1, +2, +3 … etc. We instead now have a separate arrow for each natural number instead of objects. Composition was like multiplication, but really it was addition of natural numbers in the exponent: fn ◦ fm = fn+m.

By now, we have seen three ways of putting category structure on natural numbers:

  1. Using factors
  2. Using size
  3. Using addition

In the first two, numbers were objects. How arrows formed were different. Now, in third case, we assumed one object and mapped everything into the arrows instead. So, this is a different abstraction that is really powerful.

Definition

A category with only one object is called a monoid.

Consequences

Since there is just one object, all arrows are composable. Now, coming back to definition of binary operation, composition is generalization of binary operation. So, when there is just one object, composition is a binary operation on the arrows.

Non categorical definition

A monoid is a set M equipped with an identity 1 and a unital and associative binary operation ◦. The monoid is sometimes written fully as (M, ◦, 1).

  • unital means that for all m ∈ M, 1 ◦ m = m = m ◦ 1
  • associativity means that for all a, b, c ∈ M, (a ◦ b) ◦ c = a ◦ (b ◦ c)

Relation between these two

Objects of monoid
Single Dummy object and arrows
Identity object
Identity arrow
Binary operation
Composition
Unitality
Unitality
Associativity
Associativity

In such case where there is one object, we really don’t give importance to the object and make it all about the arrows and composability.

Conclusion

  • Natural numbers are monoid under addition. Free monoid on one generator. One object, one loop and its repeated composition makes a new arrow.
  • Now coming to mod(n) category, we impose extra rules because it loops on itself like f5 = f4 . f = 1 . f = f . So, these extra loops on mod(4) so this becomes a monoid but with constraint f4 = 1 which makes it integer mod(4). This can be generalized to Zn with fn = 1 since it loops on itself it won’t need two different kind of relationships to get all numbers. e.g. For natural numbers, we cant get to negative numbers by just addition. But, in this case, since it loops after a certain point, they become composable for integers as well. Such a beautiful concept.

Groups and Groupoids

  • Integers are different from natural numbers in having negative numbers, which are inverses with respect to addition, also called “additive inverses”.
  • Inverses undo the binary operation wrt that element, taking back to identity.
  • An inverse for an element a of a monoid (M, ◦, 1) is an element b such that a ◦ b = 1 and b ◦ a = 1.
  • In general definition of monoids, they don’t have inverses for every element. If a monoid does, then that’s a special case. In case of normal natural numbers under addition, only 0 has a additive inverse. Others don’t. But, in mod operation under integers Zn, there are inverses for each element.
    • e.g. in mod(4) we have inverses like this:
      • 0 – 0
      • 1 – 3
      • 2 – 2
      • 3 – 1
  • Now, coming back to monoidal representation: The arrow fk has inverse fn−k since fk ◦ fn−k = fn = 1.

Definition

Group is a monoid in which every element has an inverse.

Non categorical definition

A group consists of a set G equipped with a binary operation ◦ and an identity element 1 satisfying unit laws and associativity, and such that every element has an inverse with respect to ◦

Note that in a category coming from an equivalence relation the arrows are restricted — there can be at most one from any object a to an object b. By contrast in a category coming from a group the objects are restricted: there is just one, the “dummy” object. This is the main idea.

Tables arising from binary operation on a group are called Cayley tables. In such tables, each element appears once in each row and each column. Used to represent small categorical relationships.

Extras

  • Groups are often introduced directly via symmetry. Two symmetries of a given shape can be combined to produce another symmetry of that shape, and that structure forms a group.
  • Symmetry doesn’t have to be visual. e.g. in x2 + 2xy + y2 = 0, x and y can be interchanged and that’s symmetry in equations. Such group theory is called algebraic group theory.
  • Algebraic topology starts from the idea that you can take a topological space and encapsulate some of its structure as a group.
  • Algebraic geometry comes from studying geometry by encapsulating some of its structure as a group.
  • Algebraic number theory studies numbers via group structures.

Defining a groupoid

  • A groupoid is a category in which every arrow has an inverse. Not expecting it to be a monoid, but expecting it to have inverses.
  • Thus, by implying and relaxing certain conditions, we get different types of category.

Points and Paths

  • Now studying shapes and shape of space.
  • Topology studies what makes the shape of one space really different from the shape of another.
    • e.g. If you just moved a wall inwards slightly then the size of the space would change but in some sense not really the shape. Likewise if you shrank the entire building.
  • Given space X, we can make category with:
    • objects : points in X
    • arrows : arrow a -> b is a path from a to b in that space
  • Now comes the question: how do we say if two paths are different, and hwo do we get a composition on these paths.
  • There comes the definition of homotopy to define what really counts as same path. It tries to see if the paths by continuous deformation can go from one to another without breaking or not. If it doesn’t break, then those paths would be counted as same, etc. etc.
  • So, we just wanted to see that we can create category to study topology as well.

Chapter 12 Sets and Functions

  • A first example of large category of mathematical structure.
  • By zooming out, we study larger structures.
  • Poset is a set of objects equipped with some ordering on it. So, the collection of all possible posets is also a category.
  • From one smaller mathematical structure, we built a larger structure. Same can be done for monoids, groups, spaces etc. And the starting point for all these structures is an underlying set.
  • So, sets are special in some way and then the maps between structures is then concept of a function.

Comparisons with set theory
