item.title: The Courage of Being Disliked
item.description:
Notes

  • None of us live in an objective world, but instead in a subjective world that we ourselves have given meaning to. The world you see is different from the one I see, and it’s impossible to share your world with anyone else.
  • If environments condition people, all those who had bad parents must turn the same way.
  • “Past doesn’t matter.” according to Alderian Psychology.
  • Teleology: Study of purpose of a given phenomenon rather than study of causation (etiology). Your friend had the goal of not going out beforehand, and he’s been manufacturing a state of anxiety and fear as a means to achieve that goal.
  • We make out of trauma whatever suits our purposes. Experiences don’t determine but the meaning we give them is self-determining.
  • Immediate rewards for people: e.g. He is creating anxiety and fear as his reasons to stay inside. It’s not that the person is happy or satisfied but there’s no doubt that person is acting in alignment to his/her goal.
  • People get angry that they could shout.
  • People anticipate things that the other person will say, the measures they will take to correct their mistake and humble apology. But, people want to shout and they shout. This is way you show your power over others. You used emotion of anger as tool to make the other person submit to you.
  • Mother, principal, call, anger as a choice, anger to overpower child with loud voice thus assert her opinions.
  • People have emotions but they have control over it.
  • If past would only determine everyone’s future, we would end up with nihilism and pessimism losing any hope.
  • People think their disposition or personality cannot be changed. In Adlerian psychology, we describe personality and disposition with the word “lifestyle." Lifestyle is a word that encompasses the worldview of that person and his or her outlook on life.
  • Example of How personality can be reformed: Say there’s someone who worries about himself and says, “I am a pessimist.” One could rephrase that to instead say, “I have a pessimistic view of the world.” You could consider that the issue is not personality but rather the view of the world. It seems that the word “personality” is nuanced and suggests being unchangeable. But if we’re talking about a view of the world, well, then, that should be possible to alter.
  • You probably think that lifestyle you have is the most practical one and it’s easier to leave things as they are.
  • Changing lifestyle needs courage. Anxiety generated by changing vs Disappointment of not changing. Most people go for the latter.

Examples

Novelist

  • An aspiring novelist says job keeps him too busy and he can never find time to write novels. He does all this because he wants to leave the possibility: “I can do it if I try.”

Girl and Fear of Blushing

  • She fabricated that fear of blushing as an excuse for her own inability to confess her feelings. Or maybe as a kind of insurance for when he rejected her.
  • Fear of blushing makes you accept your dissatisfaction with world around you and a life that isn’t going well. If by getting this fear out, you’d probably come back and say “Give me my fear of blushing which can’t be done.”
  • When she didn’t need it, she just went away with it. The guy she liked confessed and there was no need of dealing with it anymore.

Notes

  • We similarly are afraid of being negated by other people. We are afraid of being refused and sustaining deep mental wounds.
  • It’s impossible to not get hurt in relations with other people. “To get rid of one’s problems, all one can do is live in the universe all alone”
  • You were so afraid of interpersonal relationships that you came to dislike yourself. You’ve avoided interpersonal relationships by disliking yourself.
  • Subjectivity matters: The choice to view height either as advantage or disadvantage is open to you. It can be disadvantageous to some and advantageous to some.
  • Pursuit of superiority : People are born helpless. People have universal desire to escape from that helpless state.
  • Feeling of inferiority : Everyone is in “condition of wanting to improve”.
  • Both feelings are perfectly normal. Both can promote striving and growth if used in the right way.

Complex :

  • Abnormal mental state made up of complicated group of emotions and ideas.
  • Example: If one has feeling of inferiority about one’s education –> One can take two steps:
    • Try harder than anyone else
    • Use feeling of inferiority as kind of excuse. i.e. Complex
  • Person not marrying due to parent’s divorce in childhood simply is scared to take even one step forward. You don’t have courage to change your lifestyle.

Superiority Complex :

  • One can’t tolerate inferiority complex of thinking. A is the situation, B cannot be done. One can’t accept one’s incapable self.
  • E.g. Excessive allegiance to brands of clothing as forms of giving authority, misrepresenting one’s work etc.
  • Such people are trying to look bigger on borrowed power.
  • The one who boasts does only out of feeling of inferiority.
  • Person who boasts their upbringing, misfortunes; if you try to suggest some helping hand and change, they refuse it by saying “You don’t understand how I feel.”

Notes

  • People don’t want to change and don’t take suggestions saying that the other person doesn’t know what he/she is going through.
  • People use misfortune to control another party with it. By declaring how suffered they are, they are trying to worry people around them and restrict their behavior, speech and control them.
  • The strongest person in our culture is baby. It is because noone can control a baby.
  • A healthy feeling of inferiority is something that comes from comparison with one’s ideal self.
  • A competitor if is a comrade to you, it brings self improvement.
  • Competition at the center of interpersonal relationships cannot escape misfortune.
  • When one is conscious of competition and victory and defeat, it is inevitable that feelings of inferiority will arise. Superior and inferiority complex are extensions of that.
  • There is a difference between personal anger (personal grudge) and indignation with regard to society’s contradictions and injustices (righteous indignation). Personal anger soon cools but righteous indignation lasts for a long time.

Dealing with anger

  • Think about that person’s hidden goal.
  • Clarify if person is challenging you to a power struggle.

Personal attacks and Power struggle

  • Discussion –> Heated argument –> If neither accepts differences of opinion –> Personal attacks.
  • Even if you win the debate, competitor rushes on to the next stage.
  • When interpersonal relations reach revenge stage, it is almost impossible for either party to find a solution. One must never allow oneself to a power struggle.
  • Idea that your are bearing personal attacks is proof that you are in power struggle. Do not seek action with a reaction. That’s the only thing we can do.
  • Anger is to convey our thoughts and intentions. Learning this, anger will disappear on it’s own.
  • Irascible poeple don’t have short temper. They have no better communication tool than anger.
  • In every instance, however right you are, never try to criticize others based on that. People fall into this trap the most.
  • The moment one is convinced “One is right”, one has already entered into power struggle.
  • If you think you’re right regardless of what other’s opinion might be, close it then and there. Don’t try to make them submit.
  • Admitting mistakes means stepping down from power struggle: not defeat. Superiority should not be pursued through competition with others.

Objectives of human behavior and psychology

  • For behavior: a. Be self reliant b. Live in harmony with society
  • For psychology that supports these behaviors: a. I have the ability. b. The consciousness that people are my comrades.

How to achieve these? ==> Life tasks

  • Classification of life tasks:
    • Tasks of work
      • No choice but to confront when to live as a social being.
      • Work cannot be completed all by oneself.
      • Interpersonal relationships of work are lowest bar hurdles because of clear objective of getting good results. So, people work together even if they don’t always get along.
      • Persons tripped up in this stage are “NEETs”: young person not in education, training or employment / shut-ins (person confined indoors).
    • Tasks of friendship
    • Tasks of Love
      • Relationships in which people restrict each other eventually fall apart.
      • One should not have feeling of inferiority or need of boasting when with the person they love.
      • Types:
        • Love relationships : Connected by a red string
        • Relationships with family (particularly parent-child relation): Connected by rigid chains
      • You have a small pair of scissors for both. Even if you have to cut it, you have to face it. Worst you can do is to just stand still with situation as it is.
      • People first build the goal of disliking the person and then find flaws to satisfy that goal. People find things irritating that they lived with for so long.

Life Lies: Coming up with manner of pretexts to avoid life tasks

  • It’s the issue of courage not right or wrong between life tasks and life lies.
  • Mind and body are separate but when I fly into rage and shout, its “I as a whole” that’s shouting.
  • When people separate “I” from the “shouting emotion”, that becomes a life lie.
  • An adult, who has chosen unfree way of life, on seeing young person living freely at the moment, as hedonistic. This is life-lie that comes out when he/she cannot accept his/her unfree life. A free adult will cheer for it.

Reward-Punishment education and Separation of Tasks

  • People seek recognition due to this behavior.
  • Wishing hard to be recognized will lead to a life of following expectations held by other people who want you to be “this kind of person”.
  • Don’t behave without regard for others but there is a concept called “separation of tasks”
  • When one is confronted with task of studying, we consider it from perspective “Whose task is this?” For a child, it’s child’s task whether he/she studies or plays out. Parents commanding child to study is intruding another person’s task. People need to separate one’s own tasks from other people’s tasks.
  • All interpersonal problems arise by intruding other’s tasks or having own tasks intruded on.
  • How to know whose task it is? –> Ask “Who ultimately is going to receive result brought by the choice that is made?”
  • It’s true that one often hears parents today using the phrase “It’s for your own good.” But they are clearly doing so in order to fulfill their own goals, which could be their appearance in the eyes of society, their need to put on airs, or their desire for control, for example.
  • One has to pay attention. Though it seems like this approach is noninterference, it’s not. Noninterference is attitude of not knowing, not even being interested in knowing what child is doing. Instead, it is by knowing that one protects him/her. If problem is studying, one tells child that it’s his/her task and lets him/her know that one is ready to assist him/her when he/she has the urge to study. One must not intrude child’s task.
  • Follow: “You can head a horse to drink but you can’t make it drink.”
  • Hypothetical Example: Child locks in, what would you do? Ask whose task it is. It’s the child’s task. I would not intervene into it or focus too much of my attention into it. I would send message that I was ready to assist him whenever child is in need. Now, child has to act upon it. So, child will probably come back and ask for assistance, also trying to work some things on his/her own.
  • Closer the family, the more consciously should tasks be separated.
  • Act of believing is also a task. How a person acts with regard to your expectations and trust is other people’s task. Intervening in other’s tasks and intervening on other’s tasks will lead to life full of hardships.
  • Parents not approving your work is their task not yours.
  • People’s judgment over a choice is task of other people and you can do nothing about it.
  • Saying I have an awful boss, so I can’t work is etiology. From teleological view: I don’t want to work, so I create an awful boss. I can’t acknowledge my incapable self, so I create an awful boss.
  • Separation of tasks is not the objective of interpersonal relationships. It’s the gateway.
  • Forming good relationships requires a certain degree of distance. When distance is too small and people get stuck together, it’s impossible to even speak to each other.
  • No matter what the other person does for you or sort of appeal the person makes, it’s you who decides what you should do. When reward is the base of interpersonal relationship, there’s a feeling “I gave this much, so you should give that much back.”
  • It would be easier to intervene on certain tasks such as a child having hard time trying in tying his/her shoes. For busy mom, it’s easier to take task away and tie it herself. Repeated intervention will result in child not learning and wouldn’t confront challenges later in life.
  • Separating one’s tasks is not an egocentric thing. Intervening in other people’s tasks is essentially an egocentric way of thinking, however. Parents force their children to study; they meddle in their life and marriage choices. That is nothing other than an egocentric way of thinking.
  • Desire for recognition is a natural desire. We humans are capable of resisting default fallback modes. So, don’t let the stone roll naturally downhill.
  • Cost of freedom in interpersonal relationships is being disliked by other people.
  • One neither prepares to be self-righteous or defiant. One just separates tasks. One moves forward without fearing possibility of being disliked. This is truly freedom in terms of way of living.
  • Not wanting to be disliked is my task but whether so-and-so dislikes me is not my task.
  • Philosopher, father issues: I didn’t change in order to change my father. That is notion of manipulating other person. You don’t know what will happen to other person as result and that’s not the aspect you take part in.
  • In times, people change tandem with your change but it’s not because of your change. That is not the goal. If the other person doesn’t change, it doesn’t matter then.

Goal of interpersonal relationships: Community Feeling

  • Seeing other people as our comrades
  • Community is not just household, school, workplace, society or even nations and humanity but entire axis of time from past to the future, all plants, animals and even inanimate objects.
  • People who are obsessed with a desire for recognition will seem to be looking at other people while they are actually looking only at themselves.
  • “I” is the protagonist in one’s life. But “I” doesn’t rule the center of the world. “I” is never more than a member of community and part of a whole.
  • People obsessed with themselves, for them others means only those “who will do something” for them.
  • In Alderian psychology, sense of belonging is something that can be attained by making active commitment to community of one’s own accord, not by being here.
  • Rather than what will the person give me ? What can I give to this person? This is commitment to the community.
  • It’s natural that when we search for a sense of belonging, we will be attracted to the smaller community.
  • We search for sense of belonging here and there. Rather than not finding your sense of belonging and shrinking to smaller fo of community such as from school to shutting yourself to home, you can find you belong elsewhere if you see whole world is for you to belong.
  • When you run into difficulties with interpersonal relations and no longer see a way out, “Listen to the voice of the larger community.”
  • Living in fear of one’s relationships falling apart is an unfree way to live, in which one is living for other people.

Horizontal Relationships

  • A relation of equals. You don’t seem to be above or below someone else.
  • A parent also must not make a child feel that he/she is in a vertical relationship.
  • In child rearing, one must not praise. Physical punishment, rebuking is out of the course obviously. By praising “passing of judgment by a person of ability to a person of no ability”, it’s taking place. e.g. Mother says to a child helping her “You are a good helper.” but not to her husband. This is unconsciously creating hierarchical relationships and seeing child as beneath her.
  • Whether we praise or rebuke, background goal is manipulation. Reward-punishment education’s intention is to manipulate children.
  • All relationships should be horizontal as per Alderian psychology.
  • If one can build horizontal relationships “equal but not the same” for all people, there is no room for inferiority complexes to emerge.
  • People intervene because of vertical relationships.
  • Assistance and intervention are two different things. Assistance presupposes separation of tasks and horizontal relationships.
  • If one is not following through one’s own tasks, it’s not because of ability but because of lack of courage to face one’s tasks. So, all we do is give them courage to work on their task.
  • The more one is praised by another person, the more one forms the belief that one has no ability.
  • The most important thing is to not judge other people. “Judgment” is a word that comes out of vertical relationships. If one is building horizontal relationships, there will be words of more straightforward gratitude and respect and joy.
  • The goal is to be able to say “I can make contributions to other people”.
  • Context matters the most. If your life were in danger, and you were hanging on by a thread, the people around you would probably feel very gladdened just by the very fact of your existing. They would simply feel thankful that you are safe in the here and now, and would not be wanting you to perform some direct act.
  • People have ideal disposition and subtract scores from that ideal to judge a person. Instead of taking points away from ideal image, people could start from zero. Then, the mere existence is grateful.
  • If you are building even one vertical relationship with someone, you will be treating all your interpersonal relationships as vertical.
  • Even if you are not treating them in a boss-or-subordinate kind of way, it is as if you are saying, “A is above me, and B is below me,” for example, or “I’ll follow A’s advice, but ignore what B says,” or “I don’t mind breaking my promise to C.” This is what happens.
  • People have a space to refuse and a space to propose better way of doing things. We feel there is no space for all of it so that we can avoid conflict and responsibility.
  • There is no need to go out of one’s way to be positive and affirm oneself. It’s not self-affirmation that we are concerned with, but self-acceptance.
  • Switch from attachment to self –> concern for others requires three things:
    • Self-acceptance
      • Self-affirmation is making suggestions to oneself when something is beyond one’s ability. It can bring superiority complex. Self-acceptance is accepting a person’s incapable self and moving forward to do best that can be done.
    • Confidence in others
      • Trust vs Confidence: Trust comes with set conditions. We refer to it as credit. Bank borrows you money based on trust that you can pay back this much of money. Confidence is doing without any set conditions whatsoever when believing in others. Even if someone doesn’t have objective grounds for trust, one believes.
      • In Alderian psychology, basis of interpersonal relationships is founded not on trust but on confidence.
      • In times, people who believe unconditionally gets taken advantage of. The attitude of continuing to believe in someone even in such instances is what we call confidence.
      • Believing unconditionally doesn’t have moral significance here. It’s to make interpersonal relationship with the person better and build a horizontal relationship.
      • Don’t just focus on the wounds that people give by believing in them. In long run, you will have many deep relationships if you try this.
      • Courage to overcome fear of being taken advantage of comes from self-acceptance. If you see as taking advantage is other person’s task, getting to core of confidence in others becomes less difficult.
      • Placing confidence in others is connected to seeing other people as comrades.
    • Contribution to others
      • Contribution to others doesn’t mean self-sacrifice. People who sacrifice too much are conformed to society too much.
      • e.g. If you do all the household work in a family, you normally ask yourself these questions: Why don’t they give me a hand? Why do I have to do all the work? I should have at least received a Thank You from them. If I hum like this, I am probably not much fun to be around. If I am enjoying it, someone might come and give a hand.
      • You need to be creating an atmosphere in which its easier to offer help.
  • These three go in circle. You accept yourself thereby can have confidence in others. You have confidence, you see others as comrades. Now, you can engage in contributing to others. This gives feeling of “I am of use to someone” and it helps accept oneself as one is. And the circle repeats.
  • Stammering, feeling of inferiority, become too self conscious as a result, tipping words more and more.
  • People are aware of their worth only when they feel “I am of use to someone”. One just needs a subjective sense of it. Happiness is a feeling of contribution.
  • Pursuit of easy superiority: Child who engages in problem behavior are trying to attract attention of other people even as they continue to avoid any such healthy effort. “Revenge” and “pursuit of easy superiority” are easily linked. One makes trouble for another person while trying at the same time to be “special.”
  • People can’t accept normal self. People want to feel special. The old way doesn’t work and they make huge leap of being especially bad - the opposite.
  • Being normal is not being incapable. One doesn’t need to flaunt superiority.
  • Life is a series of dots. It’s a series of moments what you felt like a continuous line. A series of moments called ’now’. Our lives only exist in the moments. If life were a line, life planning would be possible. Since it’s a series of dots, it’s impossible to plan next.
  • The life that lies ahead of you is a completely blank page, and there are no tracks that have been laid for you to follow. There’s no story there.
  • The greatest life lie of all is not to live here and now. Believing that you know how the line goes is the biggest lie.
  • So life in general has no meaning whatsoever. But you can assign meaning to that life. And you are the only one who can assign meaning to your life.
  • You are lost in your life. Why are you lost? You are lost because you are trying to choose freedom, that is to say, a path on which you are not afraid of being disliked by others and you are not living others’ lives—a path that is yours alone.
  • In Alderian psychology, the guiding star to happiness is “Contribution to others”
  • One more time, I give you the words of Adler: “Someone has to start. Other people might not be cooperative, but that is not connected to you. My advice is this: You should start. With no regard to whether others are cooperative or not.”

item.content:
Notes

  • None of us live in an objective world, but instead in a subjective world that we ourselves have given meaning to. The world you see is different from the one I see, and it’s impossible to share your world with anyone else.
  • If environments condition people, all those who had bad parents must turn the same way.
  • “Past doesn’t matter.” according to Alderian Psychology.
  • Teleology: Study of purpose of a given phenomenon rather than study of causation (etiology). Your friend had the goal of not going out beforehand, and he’s been manufacturing a state of anxiety and fear as a means to achieve that goal.
  • We make out of trauma whatever suits our purposes. Experiences don’t determine but the meaning we give them is self-determining.
  • Immediate rewards for people: e.g. He is creating anxiety and fear as his reasons to stay inside. It’s not that the person is happy or satisfied but there’s no doubt that person is acting in alignment to his/her goal.
  • People get angry that they could shout.
  • People anticipate things that the other person will say, the measures they will take to correct their mistake and humble apology. But, people want to shout and they shout. This is way you show your power over others. You used emotion of anger as tool to make the other person submit to you.
  • Mother, principal, call, anger as a choice, anger to overpower child with loud voice thus assert her opinions.
  • People have emotions but they have control over it.
  • If past would only determine everyone’s future, we would end up with nihilism and pessimism losing any hope.
  • People think their disposition or personality cannot be changed. In Adlerian psychology, we describe personality and disposition with the word “lifestyle." Lifestyle is a word that encompasses the worldview of that person and his or her outlook on life.
  • Example of How personality can be reformed: Say there’s someone who worries about himself and says, “I am a pessimist.” One could rephrase that to instead say, “I have a pessimistic view of the world.” You could consider that the issue is not personality but rather the view of the world. It seems that the word “personality” is nuanced and suggests being unchangeable. But if we’re talking about a view of the world, well, then, that should be possible to alter.
  • You probably think that lifestyle you have is the most practical one and it’s easier to leave things as they are.
  • Changing lifestyle needs courage. Anxiety generated by changing vs Disappointment of not changing. Most people go for the latter.

Examples

Novelist

  • An aspiring novelist says job keeps him too busy and he can never find time to write novels. He does all this because he wants to leave the possibility: “I can do it if I try.”

Girl and Fear of Blushing

  • She fabricated that fear of blushing as an excuse for her own inability to confess her feelings. Or maybe as a kind of insurance for when he rejected her.
  • Fear of blushing makes you accept your dissatisfaction with world around you and a life that isn’t going well. If by getting this fear out, you’d probably come back and say “Give me my fear of blushing which can’t be done.”
  • When she didn’t need it, she just went away with it. The guy she liked confessed and there was no need of dealing with it anymore.

Notes

  • We similarly are afraid of being negated by other people. We are afraid of being refused and sustaining deep mental wounds.
  • It’s impossible to not get hurt in relations with other people. “To get rid of one’s problems, all one can do is live in the universe all alone”
  • You were so afraid of interpersonal relationships that you came to dislike yourself. You’ve avoided interpersonal relationships by disliking yourself.
  • Subjectivity matters: The choice to view height either as advantage or disadvantage is open to you. It can be disadvantageous to some and advantageous to some.
  • Pursuit of superiority : People are born helpless. People have universal desire to escape from that helpless state.
  • Feeling of inferiority : Everyone is in “condition of wanting to improve”.
  • Both feelings are perfectly normal. Both can promote striving and growth if used in the right way.

Complex :

  • Abnormal mental state made up of complicated group of emotions and ideas.
  • Example: If one has feeling of inferiority about one’s education –> One can take two steps:
    • Try harder than anyone else
    • Use feeling of inferiority as kind of excuse. i.e. Complex
  • Person not marrying due to parent’s divorce in childhood simply is scared to take even one step forward. You don’t have courage to change your lifestyle.

Superiority Complex :

  • One can’t tolerate inferiority complex of thinking. A is the situation, B cannot be done. One can’t accept one’s incapable self.
  • E.g. Excessive allegiance to brands of clothing as forms of giving authority, misrepresenting one’s work etc.
  • Such people are trying to look bigger on borrowed power.
  • The one who boasts does only out of feeling of inferiority.
  • Person who boasts their upbringing, misfortunes; if you try to suggest some helping hand and change, they refuse it by saying “You don’t understand how I feel.”

Notes

  • People don’t want to change and don’t take suggestions saying that the other person doesn’t know what he/she is going through.
  • People use misfortune to control another party with it. By declaring how suffered they are, they are trying to worry people around them and restrict their behavior, speech and control them.
  • The strongest person in our culture is baby. It is because noone can control a baby.
  • A healthy feeling of inferiority is something that comes from comparison with one’s ideal self.
  • A competitor if is a comrade to you, it brings self improvement.
  • Competition at the center of interpersonal relationships cannot escape misfortune.
  • When one is conscious of competition and victory and defeat, it is inevitable that feelings of inferiority will arise. Superior and inferiority complex are extensions of that.
  • There is a difference between personal anger (personal grudge) and indignation with regard to society’s contradictions and injustices (righteous indignation). Personal anger soon cools but righteous indignation lasts for a long time.

Dealing with anger

  • Think about that person’s hidden goal.
  • Clarify if person is challenging you to a power struggle.

Personal attacks and Power struggle

  • Discussion –> Heated argument –> If neither accepts differences of opinion –> Personal attacks.
  • Even if you win the debate, competitor rushes on to the next stage.
  • When interpersonal relations reach revenge stage, it is almost impossible for either party to find a solution. One must never allow oneself to a power struggle.
  • Idea that your are bearing personal attacks is proof that you are in power struggle. Do not seek action with a reaction. That’s the only thing we can do.
  • Anger is to convey our thoughts and intentions. Learning this, anger will disappear on it’s own.
  • Irascible poeple don’t have short temper. They have no better communication tool than anger.
  • In every instance, however right you are, never try to criticize others based on that. People fall into this trap the most.
  • The moment one is convinced “One is right”, one has already entered into power struggle.
  • If you think you’re right regardless of what other’s opinion might be, close it then and there. Don’t try to make them submit.
  • Admitting mistakes means stepping down from power struggle: not defeat. Superiority should not be pursued through competition with others.

Objectives of human behavior and psychology

  • For behavior: a. Be self reliant b. Live in harmony with society
  • For psychology that supports these behaviors: a. I have the ability. b. The consciousness that people are my comrades.

How to achieve these? ==> Life tasks

  • Classification of life tasks:
    • Tasks of work
      • No choice but to confront when to live as a social being.
      • Work cannot be completed all by oneself.
      • Interpersonal relationships of work are lowest bar hurdles because of clear objective of getting good results. So, people work together even if they don’t always get along.
      • Persons tripped up in this stage are “NEETs”: young person not in education, training or employment / shut-ins (person confined indoors).
    • Tasks of friendship
    • Tasks of Love
      • Relationships in which people restrict each other eventually fall apart.
      • One should not have feeling of inferiority or need of boasting when with the person they love.
      • Types:
        • Love relationships : Connected by a red string
        • Relationships with family (particularly parent-child relation): Connected by rigid chains
      • You have a small pair of scissors for both. Even if you have to cut it, you have to face it. Worst you can do is to just stand still with situation as it is.
      • People first build the goal of disliking the person and then find flaws to satisfy that goal. People find things irritating that they lived with for so long.

Life Lies: Coming up with manner of pretexts to avoid life tasks

  • It’s the issue of courage not right or wrong between life tasks and life lies.
  • Mind and body are separate but when I fly into rage and shout, its “I as a whole” that’s shouting.
  • When people separate “I” from the “shouting emotion”, that becomes a life lie.
  • An adult, who has chosen unfree way of life, on seeing young person living freely at the moment, as hedonistic. This is life-lie that comes out when he/she cannot accept his/her unfree life. A free adult will cheer for it.

Reward-Punishment education and Separation of Tasks

  • People seek recognition due to this behavior.
  • Wishing hard to be recognized will lead to a life of following expectations held by other people who want you to be “this kind of person”.
  • Don’t behave without regard for others but there is a concept called “separation of tasks”
  • When one is confronted with task of studying, we consider it from perspective “Whose task is this?” For a child, it’s child’s task whether he/she studies or plays out. Parents commanding child to study is intruding another person’s task. People need to separate one’s own tasks from other people’s tasks.
  • All interpersonal problems arise by intruding other’s tasks or having own tasks intruded on.
  • How to know whose task it is? –> Ask “Who ultimately is going to receive result brought by the choice that is made?”
  • It’s true that one often hears parents today using the phrase “It’s for your own good.” But they are clearly doing so in order to fulfill their own goals, which could be their appearance in the eyes of society, their need to put on airs, or their desire for control, for example.
  • One has to pay attention. Though it seems like this approach is noninterference, it’s not. Noninterference is attitude of not knowing, not even being interested in knowing what child is doing. Instead, it is by knowing that one protects him/her. If problem is studying, one tells child that it’s his/her task and lets him/her know that one is ready to assist him/her when he/she has the urge to study. One must not intrude child’s task.
  • Follow: “You can head a horse to drink but you can’t make it drink.”
  • Hypothetical Example: Child locks in, what would you do? Ask whose task it is. It’s the child’s task. I would not intervene into it or focus too much of my attention into it. I would send message that I was ready to assist him whenever child is in need. Now, child has to act upon it. So, child will probably come back and ask for assistance, also trying to work some things on his/her own.
  • Closer the family, the more consciously should tasks be separated.
  • Act of believing is also a task. How a person acts with regard to your expectations and trust is other people’s task. Intervening in other’s tasks and intervening on other’s tasks will lead to life full of hardships.
  • Parents not approving your work is their task not yours.
  • People’s judgment over a choice is task of other people and you can do nothing about it.
  • Saying I have an awful boss, so I can’t work is etiology. From teleological view: I don’t want to work, so I create an awful boss. I can’t acknowledge my incapable self, so I create an awful boss.
  • Separation of tasks is not the objective of interpersonal relationships. It’s the gateway.
  • Forming good relationships requires a certain degree of distance. When distance is too small and people get stuck together, it’s impossible to even speak to each other.
  • No matter what the other person does for you or sort of appeal the person makes, it’s you who decides what you should do. When reward is the base of interpersonal relationship, there’s a feeling “I gave this much, so you should give that much back.”
  • It would be easier to intervene on certain tasks such as a child having hard time trying in tying his/her shoes. For busy mom, it’s easier to take task away and tie it herself. Repeated intervention will result in child not learning and wouldn’t confront challenges later in life.
  • Separating one’s tasks is not an egocentric thing. Intervening in other people’s tasks is essentially an egocentric way of thinking, however. Parents force their children to study; they meddle in their life and marriage choices. That is nothing other than an egocentric way of thinking.
  • Desire for recognition is a natural desire. We humans are capable of resisting default fallback modes. So, don’t let the stone roll naturally downhill.
  • Cost of freedom in interpersonal relationships is being disliked by other people.
  • One neither prepares to be self-righteous or defiant. One just separates tasks. One moves forward without fearing possibility of being disliked. This is truly freedom in terms of way of living.
  • Not wanting to be disliked is my task but whether so-and-so dislikes me is not my task.
  • Philosopher, father issues: I didn’t change in order to change my father. That is notion of manipulating other person. You don’t know what will happen to other person as result and that’s not the aspect you take part in.
  • In times, people change tandem with your change but it’s not because of your change. That is not the goal. If the other person doesn’t change, it doesn’t matter then.

Goal of interpersonal relationships: Community Feeling

  • Seeing other people as our comrades
  • Community is not just household, school, workplace, society or even nations and humanity but entire axis of time from past to the future, all plants, animals and even inanimate objects.
  • People who are obsessed with a desire for recognition will seem to be looking at other people while they are actually looking only at themselves.
  • “I” is the protagonist in one’s life. But “I” doesn’t rule the center of the world. “I” is never more than a member of community and part of a whole.
  • People obsessed with themselves, for them others means only those “who will do something” for them.
  • In Alderian psychology, sense of belonging is something that can be attained by making active commitment to community of one’s own accord, not by being here.
  • Rather than what will the person give me ? What can I give to this person? This is commitment to the community.
  • It’s natural that when we search for a sense of belonging, we will be attracted to the smaller community.
  • We search for sense of belonging here and there. Rather than not finding your sense of belonging and shrinking to smaller fo of community such as from school to shutting yourself to home, you can find you belong elsewhere if you see whole world is for you to belong.
  • When you run into difficulties with interpersonal relations and no longer see a way out, “Listen to the voice of the larger community.”
  • Living in fear of one’s relationships falling apart is an unfree way to live, in which one is living for other people.

Horizontal Relationships

  • A relation of equals. You don’t seem to be above or below someone else.
  • A parent also must not make a child feel that he/she is in a vertical relationship.
  • In child rearing, one must not praise. Physical punishment, rebuking is out of the course obviously. By praising “passing of judgment by a person of ability to a person of no ability”, it’s taking place. e.g. Mother says to a child helping her “You are a good helper.” but not to her husband. This is unconsciously creating hierarchical relationships and seeing child as beneath her.
  • Whether we praise or rebuke, background goal is manipulation. Reward-punishment education’s intention is to manipulate children.
  • All relationships should be horizontal as per Alderian psychology.
  • If one can build horizontal relationships “equal but not the same” for all people, there is no room for inferiority complexes to emerge.
  • People intervene because of vertical relationships.
  • Assistance and intervention are two different things. Assistance presupposes separation of tasks and horizontal relationships.
  • If one is not following through one’s own tasks, it’s not because of ability but because of lack of courage to face one’s tasks. So, all we do is give them courage to work on their task.
  • The more one is praised by another person, the more one forms the belief that one has no ability.
  • The most important thing is to not judge other people. “Judgment” is a word that comes out of vertical relationships. If one is building horizontal relationships, there will be words of more straightforward gratitude and respect and joy.
  • The goal is to be able to say “I can make contributions to other people”.
  • Context matters the most. If your life were in danger, and you were hanging on by a thread, the people around you would probably feel very gladdened just by the very fact of your existing. They would simply feel thankful that you are safe in the here and now, and would not be wanting you to perform some direct act.
  • People have ideal disposition and subtract scores from that ideal to judge a person. Instead of taking points away from ideal image, people could start from zero. Then, the mere existence is grateful.
  • If you are building even one vertical relationship with someone, you will be treating all your interpersonal relationships as vertical.
  • Even if you are not treating them in a boss-or-subordinate kind of way, it is as if you are saying, “A is above me, and B is below me,” for example, or “I’ll follow A’s advice, but ignore what B says,” or “I don’t mind breaking my promise to C.” This is what happens.
  • People have a space to refuse and a space to propose better way of doing things. We feel there is no space for all of it so that we can avoid conflict and responsibility.
  • There is no need to go out of one’s way to be positive and affirm oneself. It’s not self-affirmation that we are concerned with, but self-acceptance.
  • Switch from attachment to self –> concern for others requires three things:
    • Self-acceptance
      • Self-affirmation is making suggestions to oneself when something is beyond one’s ability. It can bring superiority complex. Self-acceptance is accepting a person’s incapable self and moving forward to do best that can be done.
    • Confidence in others
      • Trust vs Confidence: Trust comes with set conditions. We refer to it as credit. Bank borrows you money based on trust that you can pay back this much of money. Confidence is doing without any set conditions whatsoever when believing in others. Even if someone doesn’t have objective grounds for trust, one believes.
      • In Alderian psychology, basis of interpersonal relationships is founded not on trust but on confidence.
      • In times, people who believe unconditionally gets taken advantage of. The attitude of continuing to believe in someone even in such instances is what we call confidence.
      • Believing unconditionally doesn’t have moral significance here. It’s to make interpersonal relationship with the person better and build a horizontal relationship.
      • Don’t just focus on the wounds that people give by believing in them. In long run, you will have many deep relationships if you try this.
      • Courage to overcome fear of being taken advantage of comes from self-acceptance. If you see as taking advantage is other person’s task, getting to core of confidence in others becomes less difficult.
      • Placing confidence in others is connected to seeing other people as comrades.
    • Contribution to others
      • Contribution to others doesn’t mean self-sacrifice. People who sacrifice too much are conformed to society too much.
      • e.g. If you do all the household work in a family, you normally ask yourself these questions: Why don’t they give me a hand? Why do I have to do all the work? I should have at least received a Thank You from them. If I hum like this, I am probably not much fun to be around. If I am enjoying it, someone might come and give a hand.
      • You need to be creating an atmosphere in which its easier to offer help.
  • These three go in circle. You accept yourself thereby can have confidence in others. You have confidence, you see others as comrades. Now, you can engage in contributing to others. This gives feeling of “I am of use to someone” and it helps accept oneself as one is. And the circle repeats.
  • Stammering, feeling of inferiority, become too self conscious as a result, tipping words more and more.
  • People are aware of their worth only when they feel “I am of use to someone”. One just needs a subjective sense of it. Happiness is a feeling of contribution.
  • Pursuit of easy superiority: Child who engages in problem behavior are trying to attract attention of other people even as they continue to avoid any such healthy effort. “Revenge” and “pursuit of easy superiority” are easily linked. One makes trouble for another person while trying at the same time to be “special.”
  • People can’t accept normal self. People want to feel special. The old way doesn’t work and they make huge leap of being especially bad - the opposite.
  • Being normal is not being incapable. One doesn’t need to flaunt superiority.
  • Life is a series of dots. It’s a series of moments what you felt like a continuous line. A series of moments called ’now’. Our lives only exist in the moments. If life were a line, life planning would be possible. Since it’s a series of dots, it’s impossible to plan next.
  • The life that lies ahead of you is a completely blank page, and there are no tracks that have been laid for you to follow. There’s no story there.
  • The greatest life lie of all is not to live here and now. Believing that you know how the line goes is the biggest lie.
  • So life in general has no meaning whatsoever. But you can assign meaning to that life. And you are the only one who can assign meaning to your life.
  • You are lost in your life. Why are you lost? You are lost because you are trying to choose freedom, that is to say, a path on which you are not afraid of being disliked by others and you are not living others’ lives—a path that is yours alone.
  • In Alderian psychology, the guiding star to happiness is “Contribution to others”
  • One more time, I give you the words of Adler: “Someone has to start. Other people might not be cooperative, but that is not connected to you. My advice is this: You should start. With no regard to whether others are cooperative or not.”

item.title: Algorithm Design Manual
item.description:
Algorithm Design Manual

Common mistake is to use pseudocode to dress up an ill-defined idea so that it looks more formal.

For correctness of algorithms

  • Set of allowed input instances
  • Required properties of algorithm’s output.

Tips for design

  • Narrowing the set of allowable instances until there is correct and efficient algorithm. e.g. Restrict graph problem from general graph down to trees or 2d to 1d.
  • Traps in specifying output requirements:
    • Not correctly specifying what best measure is.
    • Creating compound goals which are hard to reason and solve.
  • Find counter examples:
    • Think small and simple.
    • Think exhaustively.
    • Hunt for the weakness. e.g [ Words like always and so on.]
    • Go for a tie if algorithms are greedy.
    • Take extremes: high and low, up and down, few and many, near and far.
    • Boundary errors in inductive proofs.

Defining Problem Names

  • Permutation: Arrangement, Tour, Ordering or Sequence
  • Subsets: Cluster, COllection, Committee, Group, Packaging or Selection.
  • Trees: Hierarchy, Dominance Relationship, Ancestor/Descendant Relationship or Taxonomy.
  • Graphs: Network, Web, Circuit or Relationship.
  • Points: Sites, Positions, Data Records or Locations.
  • Polygons and Polyhedra: Shapes, Regions, Configurations or Boundaries.
  • Strings: Text, Characters, Patterns or Labels.

Ways to think

  • Think recursively: Look for big problems that are made from smaller ones of same type. e.g. Remove one node from permutation and it’s permutation of one less element. Removing the root of tree gives collection of small trees.
  • Design the programs with efficient data structure in the first place.

Types of data structures by memory continuity

Contiguously-allocated

  • Single slabs of memory.
  • Arrays, matrices, Heaps and Hash tables.
  • Constant access time given the index.
  • Space efficiency due to no pointers.
  • Memory Locality helps a lot in cache memories where there will be lots of cache hits.

Linked

  • Distinct chunks of memory bound together by pointers
  • Lists, trees, Graph Adjacency Lists.
  • Complicated Deletions.

Basic Information about Data Structures

  • Effective Implementation can be using either arrays or linked lists. Key issue is whether an upper bound on the size of the container is known in advance, thus permitting the use of a statically-allocated array.
  • Dictionaries support operations such as:
    • Min(D) or Max(D)
    • Predecessor(D, k) or Successor(D, k)
  • Unsorted doubly linked lists support insertion and deletion in O(1) but search takes linear time in worst case.
  • Sorted arrays support binary search but cost of linear time update.

Binary Search Trees

  • Basic operations supported by binary trees are searching, traversal, insertion and deletion. The pre-order and post-order traversal make little sense with search trees, but prove useful when rooted tree represents arithmetic or logical expressions. Allocating the node and linking it to tree is constant-time operation after the search has been performed in O(h) time.
  • Deletion in binary trees is complicated, worst case complexity takes at most two searches which takes O(h) and constant time for pointer manipulation. It has three cases:
    • Having only one child. SOLUTION: Link grandchild to the parent.
    • Having two children. SOLUTION: Relabel the node with key of immediate successor in sorted order.
  • Balanced search trees have all dictionary operations ( Insert, Delete and Query ) taking O(logn) time.

Trying to sort using specific operations only

  1. Sort in O(n logn) time using minimum, insert, delete and search.
    • Repeatedly find and delete the minimum element to traverse the elements in sorted order.
  2. Sort in O(n logn) time using only insert and in-order traversal.
    • Insert all n elements and do in-order traversal to access the items in sorted order.
  3. Sort in O(n logn) time using only minimum, successor and insert.
    • Start with the minimum element and then repeatedly find the successor to traverse the elements in the sorted order.

Priority Queues

  • Supports three primary operations
    • Insert(Q, x)
    • Find-Minimum(Q) or Find-Maximum(Q)
    • Delete-Minimum(Q) or Delete-Maximum(Q)
  • Naturally occuring. E.g. Dating Potential Candidates with Desirability Score where you try to Find-Maximum(), spend evening to evaluate them better and maybe update their score.
  • Worst time complexity in priority Queue when underlying data structure is
Array Type/Operation Delete-Min Find-Min Insert
Unsorted Array O(n) O(n) O(1)
Sorted Array O(1) O(1) O(n)
BST O(1) O(1) O(logn)

Hashing and Strings

  • Practical way to maintain a dictionary and having constant time access.
  • Collision is the major setback in hash and can be resolved using:
    • Chaining: Having a linked list of items with same hash key. But memory taken to store pointers.
    • Open Addressing: Hash table maintained as array [ not bucket ] with each element initialised to NULL. On inserting an item, if spot is taken; takes the next possible place. Here, deleting can get ugly since removing one element might break a chain of operations. Thus, we need to reinsert all the items in the run following the new hole.
    • In m-element hash table, Chaining takes O(n+m) time for chaining and O(m) for open addressing since n must be at most m.

Effective String Matching using Hash Tables

  • Fundamental operation is substring search.
  • Searching by placing the substring over string takes O(nm) time.
  • Rabin-Karp algorithm can do it in expected linear time.
    • Hash function on both pattern string ‘p’ and m-character substring from ith position of t. Hash values will be same in case of match. Even the false-positives are so rare and can be checked for explicitly easily.
    • So, this reduces matching to n-m+2 hash value computations but since hash function takes O(m) time to compute hash function on m-character string, the computation is O(mn) again.
    • Catch is we can compute hash of one changed character in string using simple multiplication, addition and subtraction which can be done in constant time. Thus, the O(nm) time complexity reduces to O(n).

Duplicate Detection

  • Used by search engines to compare documents.
  • Hashing for bids.

Specialized data structures

  • String
  • Geometric
  • Graph
  • Set

Pragmatics of Sorting

  • What order do we want the items sorted?
    • Increasing or Decreasing Order
    • Sorting just the key or entire record
    • What should we do with equal keys?
      • Secondary Keys such as article size OR leave items in same relative order as in the original permutation.
      • Algorithms that enforce such requirement are known as Stable.
      • Right way to specify such matters is to have proper way to use comparison of records.

Heap Sort

  • What happens if we replace unsorted array in Priority Queue implementation with better data structure : Heap or Binary Search Tree? Using such implementation takes O(nlogn) instead of O(n2).
  • Heapsort is nothing but implementation of selection sort using right data structure.

item.title: Brain Facts
item.description:
Brain Physiology:

Representation

ID: 85b03664-e44a-4ba2-96f8-636cdd41b7c8

Description

  1. Cerebrum
    • Largest part of brain
  2. Corpus Callosum
    • Pathway to connect left and right hemisphere of brain
  3. Cerebral Cortex
    • Folded structure of cerebrum
  4. Frontal Lobe
    • Part of cerebral cortex just above the eyes
    • Voluntary Movement, Planning, High level Cognitive Skills such as problem solving
  5. Parietal Lobe
    • Region just behind the frontal lobe
    • Responsible for sensory processing and some visual processing
  6. Occipital Lobe
    • Part of cerebral cortex at the back of the head
    • Visual processing: Recognizing color and shapes and understanding visual input
  7. Temporal Lobe
    • Part of C.C. at the sides of the head
    • Responsible for visual processing and interpreting auditory information.
  8. Hippocampus
    • Curved structure below cerebral cortex
    • Responsible for forming memories
  9. Amygdala
    • Responsible for integrating emotions and memories
  10. Limbic System
    • Hippocampus and amygdala together
    • Responsible for regulating emotion and motivation
  11. Thalamus
    • Sensory information and relay it to other parts of the brain
  12. Forebrain
    • All these structures with cerebral cortex
  13. Midbrain
    • Beneath the thalamus
    • Coordinate eye movement such as blinking, focusing , triggering reflexes based on loud noise
    • Fine motor control skills such as writing with pen or playing a musical instrument
  14. Hindbrain
    • Glucose regulation, sleep and help control movement

  15. Basal Ganglia

  16. Cerebellum
    • Tucked underneath occipital lobe
    • Coordinate movement and learn new motor skills
  17. Pons
    • Breathing and posture control
  18. Medulla
    • Nerve pathways from brain to spinal cord

  19. Brainstem

  20. Thalamocortical loops and EEG
  21. Brain Waves Frequencies

item.title: Controlling Irrational Thoughts
item.description:
Solutions

ID: 14c476ff-c39c-47f8-a6f4-cd08e38f4ea1
  1. Mindfulness
    • Knowing what you are thinking of and what is happening internally will help you understand how irrational thoughts surface and develop with time.
    • To help with thought interruptions, keep a timer, rubber band or something that constantly stays with you and add it to your lifestyle purposefully for that mental activity interruption.
  2. Gratitude
    • Feel good for all the small yet beautiful things in life. This helps build positive hormones in the brain.
  3. Challenge irrationalities
    • When you find yourself nagging without any evidence, challenge yourself to find evidences for it. Bring logic and rationality to the picture; will help you realize the futility of a thought drain.
  4. Meditate
    • Any way of meditation is helpful for your mind since it’s the time you accept to recognize yourself without subconsciously living a life and accepting everything that’s out there. It will help you get insights, be more peaceful as well.
  5. Visualization
    • Visualization are amazing tools of positive affirmations. If you can imagine yourself doing and believe it, it will help you attract that effect. Imagine yourself being confident just like a mantra to repeat at certain times. This will push yourself to work as well.

item.title: On Procrastination
item.description:
Procrastination

ID: 2e93fc98-6218-4630-8ff0-1d30c3f6849c

Problem 1: Immensity of work

  • You commit to wiping out an entire forest instead of actually starting to work with a single tree at the moment.

  • What happens?

    • Even before starting, the mental pressure of the whole big hill over you makes you more afraid even to start. You try to console yourself that you can do it in some later point as you don’t have the energy to do it now or some reason to justify not to do it now. The immensity makes it difficult even after days.

  • Solution

    • Break down a big task into as simple tasks as possible. Like breaking down a big rock into pebbles. The pebbles should be as simple as they can be such as setting up your environment and so on.
item.content:
Procrastination

ID: 2e93fc98-6218-4630-8ff0-1d30c3f6849c

Problem 1: Immensity of work

  • You commit to wiping out an entire forest instead of actually starting to work with a single tree at the moment.

  • What happens?

    • Even before starting, the mental pressure of the whole big hill over you makes you more afraid even to start. You try to console yourself that you can do it in some later point as you don’t have the energy to do it now or some reason to justify not to do it now. The immensity makes it difficult even after days.

  • Solution

    • Break down a big task into as simple tasks as possible. Like breaking down a big rock into pebbles. The pebbles should be as simple as they can be such as setting up your environment and so on.

Problem 2: Fear of actual results

  • What happens?

    • You want to get gratification by saying: “I could have done that amazing task and I know I would be great at it”. You are taking this mental gratification as a justification for not doing the task at hand. Remember: “You can’t edit a blank page.”

  • Solution

    • If you think people will judge you for your results and you think it will make you feel bad. In fact, people don’t even care for most of us. Just because you have over 1000 friends on Facebook, hundreds of followers on Instagram doesn’t mean they are interested in you. People aren’t computers. Even the strongest of memories fade away: People have to have a grudge on you to remember small things that you failed even if you failed small. Will you care about them and not work?

Problem 3: Jumbled physical spaces

  • You watch movie, read and sleep on the same bed.

  • What happens?

    • You have no specific place that you can work on so that sitting on the space itself helps you commit to work you put off for a long time.

  • Solution :ATTACH:

    • Your mind’s accustomed to working things as automatically as you can. Creative people, players and even commonly us: We do things unconsciously upon being in different kinds of environment. Your brain’s amazing and does tasks on it’s own as much as it can. But these automatic tasks might not be favorable at instances. Your body understands to feel drowsy and sleepy when in bed; So when you feel like being the most productive person on the planet in your bed, your brain fails you miserably.

      So, instead of quarreling with the hundreds of years of evolution, take it to your advantage. If you separate spaces for your work, sleep and rest; now this habit of brain helps you to work when you are at physical space representing work: either it’s simple table and chair for you or an entire study room.

Problem 4: No actionable tasks

  • Even your planned tasks are vague and need more thinking.

  • What happens?

    • Your tasks need thinking even after you made the plan. Now you drown down the rabbit hole and the whole loop starts again.

  • Solution

    1. Two minute rule: Tasks that take two minutes now: just slash them out of your list. Your list is precious and needs to be as clean as possible. These two minutes task if ignored for now might take longer later on.
    2. Make tasks actionable: Don’t drown into thoughts again : I will do this or that and all of it. Make simple tasks that you can clearly see yourself working and start doing it.
    3. Start with something that you find best in that whole rock: a simple crystal you like. It might not be the first thing to do but to keep you on track and inspire you: it will be the best place to start.
    4. Plan tasks with actual schedule. Don’t even think of situations where you can compromise later. What if someone calls me for party? This is the worst thing you can do now. What happens and what to be done if such thing happens is to be taken care of at that very moment it happens. Don’t ever fall into that trap.

Problem 5: You are a perfectionist

  • You feel like you have to be the best out there and shouldn’t do something that’s not amazing.

  • What happens?

    • Being a perfectionist but realist at the same time helps but just making perfect imaginations of anything doesn’t help at all. Learn the art of the start. Be relentless to perfection but for god’s sake start with any output you can have.

  • Solution

    • We all want to have the best versions of ourselves to show to others. Noone wants to be seen weak or incapable. But it’s people who start with anything they have, improvise over time are the ones who accomplish the most. It’s okay to be afraid because it’s deep rooted in our brain from earlier times of evolution. It’s a social coping mechanism. People who weren’t accepted by society back in hunting days would die or be killed. We have changed but our brains are wired the same way. Don’t stress over it. Just give time to see people doing imperfect things. You can start by looking at works of your favorite YouTubers and movie stars so that you know people you thought are perfect now were not perfect from the very start. They improvised over time to be who they are now.

Problem 6: Tasks that need Internet

  • You start working with all your enthusiasm when a certain notification bell rings on your phone or you start with 10 minutes of Facebook time.

  • What happens?

    • You get lost searching for things on the internet related to your task and find at the end of the day that you spent a whole day watching YouTube videos and browsing Facebook or Reddit or anything you hadn’t planned for.

  • Solution

    • In today’s time, most of us can’t work without using internet. While all the media companies and businesses over internet are there to lure you to spend more time on their platform, it’s a very hard escape out of it. They have been studying our psychologies and preferences even those which we are not even conscious of. So, the best thing we can do is be aware. Be present at the moment. Have a stopwatch tick before you start using Internet or regular interval checks to at least know when you have plunged into it. Doing this simple act will change you over time. It’s not an overnight thing but it will create some significant changes.
    • Use site blockers: the stricter the better. Some cannot even be uninstalled after you activate them. Make sure to make it as difficult as possible to stop them. e.g. Trigger stopping it to deleting all your movies and music from your hard drive. Just giving some ideas.

Few Last Tips

  • Use Pomodoro technique if you like it. It helps make tasks look simple in terms of time to commit to tasks.
  • Use your morning to give a momentum for the day. Just accomplishing simple tasks as folding your bed or cleaning up your room can give you a feeling of gratitude and push you to break some more rocks ahead.
  • Getting Things Done is a nice way to organize your todo lists.
  • Try to make a weekly review of your todo list so that you know what are blocking you. You can do shorter reviews such as in 3 days. The faster the review time: the better the feedback loop. You know your problems better.

item.title: Looking Back to School Life
item.description:
A Reminiscence

Looking at this image, I find it funny how we change so much that we are no longer ourselves. I believed I was this way for as long as I can remember but alas with time: memories fade, people around you change and you no longer are the same person that you were before. This is the first page of my diary I made in my 9th grade. Looking at the aim I wrote in this diary, it feels so funny and grave misfortune that I had no idea about the storm of life that was about to burst upon me with all it’s might. I so foolishly believed life was all about being the best in exams. There’s a catch here though: the people I was around, the people who wanted me to have a bright successful life always came to me and said it: maybe thousand times or more. My teachers, my parents, my relatives and everyone that wished well for me. Either they didn’t know that life was so intricate and complex beyond you passing exams and being best out of it. I believed it to be the holy grail that would guide my life now.
item.content:
A Reminiscence

Looking at this image, I find it funny how we change so much that we are no longer ourselves. I believed I was this way for as long as I can remember but alas with time: memories fade, people around you change and you no longer are the same person that you were before. This is the first page of my diary I made in my 9th grade. Looking at the aim I wrote in this diary, it feels so funny and grave misfortune that I had no idea about the storm of life that was about to burst upon me with all it’s might. I so foolishly believed life was all about being the best in exams. There’s a catch here though: the people I was around, the people who wanted me to have a bright successful life always came to me and said it: maybe thousand times or more. My teachers, my parents, my relatives and everyone that wished well for me. Either they didn’t know that life was so intricate and complex beyond you passing exams and being best out of it. I believed it to be the holy grail that would guide my life now.

Now, Walking along this path, I did what I believed. I became the best version of who I could be with what I had. Then the wind hit me hard in my face as I faced the winding road of life. There was no simple aim in anyone’s life. I was with my shield of being best in exams and in real life I was as naked as I could be. Now, the arrows hit me from all sides: arrows being just education and certificate doesn’t make you who you want to be. Life told me: You need to learn some life skills: hobbies that you can do when you are in pain so that you get lost in yourself, skills that you can at least earn some money for your expenses, ability to ask for what you want when you realize the world doesn’t give a damn about you and the fact that you have to go exploring the world rather than success and happiness coming to you by default.

The quote I wrote there seems amazing to me since myself in that state was all clear about his life and his path. Yet, that me knew what was going to happen with my life. For all these years, this quote has been the summary of my life. I feared ever trying to give 100% to anything. I always left when I felt it was finally up to the top. I felt an urge to back down when I saw the peak. It was never that I didn’t have the knowledge or the skills I needed, it was just I was afraid of falling on the way to the mountaintop. All this has come to me after 8 years. I wished I could write this letter to that me 8 years back.Would it have mattered? Would I have listened to myself? That’s a question that will forever remain.

I have gone through a horrible path to get out of this belief. I hope no child is taught that exams are the way to better life: life is much more than that. I hope noone has to go this long to realize their beliefs were a lie.

item.title: गजल
item.description:
तिम्रो बोली गुलाबको फूल मनमा भने काँडा रैछ झुटो मेरो वचन होइन पापी तिम्रो आँखा रैछ ।

माया प्रेमको अन्धकारमा हराएको मेरो दृष्टि नयन हेर्दा निर्दोष तिमी मनमा भने ढुसी रैछ ।

सुन्दरताको मोहजालमा तड्पाएर मेरो शरीर अङ्ग भङ्ग पारी शरीर बेच्ने तिम्रो चाहा रैछ ।

जीवनको नाटककी पारङ्गत कलाकार तिमी मायाको अमृतमा लोभ्याएर विष मिसाई पीलाउनु रैछ ।

तिम्रो केशको छायाँमा नै जीवन जिउँछु भन्ने मलाई त्यै केशको फन्दा बनाई प्याक्क पारी मार्नु रैछ ।

item.title: Tentacles of Thoughts
item.description:
Inside the dark vents of my body,

Lies the vines: of growing darkness.

Trying to find it’s way to my brain,

It sweeps, explodes

It grunges from the inside.

 

There used to be garden inside,

Thoughts laid peace within me.

Fights were always physical then,

Peace was a habit,

And thoughts resembled curiosity then.

 

The darkness grew out of the worldly ways,

The stories of success,

The stories of failures,
item.content:
Inside the dark vents of my body,

Lies the vines: of growing darkness.

Trying to find it’s way to my brain,

It sweeps, explodes

It grunges from the inside.

 

There used to be garden inside,

Thoughts laid peace within me.

Fights were always physical then,

Peace was a habit,

And thoughts resembled curiosity then.

 

The darkness grew out of the worldly ways,

The stories of success,

The stories of failures,

The horrors of living,

The ephemeral life,

And the drive to thrive.

 

Now,

With a gasp it starts,

Slowly it finds it’s way

Creepy they are,

Creeping through me like swinging vines,

Stranded and clogged.

 

Walls of mind and tentacles of thoughts,

The war of the microcosm,

The dance of the devil form.

My bones are still the same,

My muscles undeformed,

But it feels like

The quarks inside them want some deadly transform.

 

Cold it is,

To fight with ownself.

Hard it is,

To break the chains of thoughts.

Pain it is,

To not understand anyone but ownself.

Peace it is,

To lay inside the box in peace

With tentacles of thoughts buried to the ground.

item.title: Peak
item.description:
Peak they saw,

Thought they made,

Of the day when their steps would be on the mountain peak,

Clear seem’d they, Of the goal they desperately seek.

 

Guided by the river trail,

Dreams flew high against the flow,

The mountains of hope: deep and strong first,

Now saw the wind of fear that slowly blow.

 

The path feels rough now,

The silent howls of people’s voice he heard,

Of those who got lost on that way,

Peak they saw,

Thought they made,

Of the day when their steps would be on the mountain peak,

Clear seem’d they, Of the goal they desperately seek.

 

Guided by the river trail,

Dreams flew high against the flow,

The mountains of hope: deep and strong first,

Now saw the wind of fear that slowly blow.

 

The path feels rough now,

The silent howls of people’s voice he heard,

Of those who got lost on that way,

And of those who sought to walk away.

 

His heart gets cold,

The body gets blue,

Creeping from the inside out,

Growls the wolf wishing to devour his vow.

item.title: My First Vipassana Experience
item.description: The journey of it starts with a recommendation from two of my friends. I, being desperate to experience something spiritual and majestic, decided to take on a 10 day Vipasana course. Being an Engineering student from tech related field, it’s quiet essential for you to cope through the old dying syllabus and find yourself some life through the Internet.
